checklist.step: Rebuild the PMIERs section-to-evidence index for the quarter
actions: Open the current PMIERs text on the Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac PMIERs pages and walk Sections 400 (Origination and Underwriting), 600-601 (Lender Approval and Monitoring) and 700 (Financial Requirements) section by section.

In the compliance evidence repository open Mortgage Guaranty / PMIERs / Readiness and add one index row per section: section number, section title, evidence artifact name, named owner, refresh frequency, last refresh date.
Mark every row touched by the 2024 Available Asset amendment with its phase-in step and the 9/30/2026 full-effectiveness date so partially phased evidence is not mistaken for final.
Send the index to the Head of Capital Management, the Underwriting Quality / Audit Manager and Vendor Management to confirm each named owner accepts their rows in writing.
File the confirmed index as PMIERs-readiness-index-<yyyy-Qn>.xlsx in the readiness folder.
checklist.done: every PMIERs section with an evidence obligation has an index row with a named, written-confirmed owner and a refresh date inside the quarter.

checklist.step: Pull the Exhibit F Quarterly Portfolio Loan Level Dataset as the readiness backbone
actions: Run the Exhibit F extract job for the quarter-end as-of date and pull the loan-level fields the Enterprises require: Enterprise loan number, certificate number, original and current LTV, representative credit score, vintage year, occupancy, property type, delinquency status bucket and risk-in-force.
Reconcile the extract's certificate count and total risk-in-force to the policy administration in-force register at the same as-of date and clear differences over 0.1% before the file is used.

Hand the reconciled extract to the Capital Management Manager as the base for the Minimum Required Assets calculation and store the same file in the readiness folder as the review-ready loan population.
Record the extract run id, row count, as-of date and reconciliation result on the readiness index row for Section 700.
checklist.done: a reconciled Exhibit F dataset for the quarter is stored in the readiness folder with run id, row count and a documented tie-out to the in-force register.

checklist.step: Assemble the lender approval evidence pack under Sections 600-601
actions: Ask Underwriting Operations for the list of lenders approved, re-certified, suspended or terminated during the quarter, with effective dates.

For each new approval pull the completed lender application, financial statements reviewed, agency approval status (Fannie Mae / Freddie Mac seller-servicer standing), licensing check, quality-control plan review and the signed master policy addendum.

For each existing lender pull the annual re-certification record and the most recent monitoring scorecard showing delinquency, rescission and QC-defect rates against the tolerance thresholds in the lender monitoring policy.
Confirm every suspension or termination decision carries a dated approval memo naming the Underwriting Director / Manager who made the call and the monitoring trigger that fired.
Index the pack by lender name and lender number and link it to the Section 600-601 index rows.
checklist.done: every lender approval, re-certification, suspension and termination in the quarter has a complete, dated file linked to the Section 600-601 index rows.

checklist.step: Assemble the Section 402 property valuation control evidence
actions: Export from the underwriting platform every insurance certificate issued in the quarter with its valuation type: full appraisal, appraisal waiver / property inspection waiver, desktop or hybrid appraisal, and the Collateral Underwriter or Loan Collateral Advisor risk score where the lender supplied one.
For the post-close QC sample, pull the appraisal PDF, the value used for the LTV calculation and the independent valuation review or AVM cascade result held on file.

Recompute original LTV = original loan amount ÷ lower of sales price and appraised value for every sampled certificate and flag any row where the platform LTV differs by more than 0.5 percentage points.
Document the written valuation policy in force during the quarter, including the eligibility rules for waiver-based valuations, and attach the version with its approval date.
Hand flagged rows to the Underwriting Director / Manager for disposition within 10 business days.
checklist.done: the valuation evidence pack holds the policy in force, the QC sample with recomputed LTVs, and a disposition for every flagged certificate.

checklist.step: Capture the Available Asset classification evidence under the 2024 amendment
actions: Export the quarter-end investment portfolio position file with CUSIP, asset class, NAIC designation or NRSRO rating, market value and liquidity classification.

Apply the amended Available Asset standard: split bonds by credit quality and liquidity tier, and separately identify holdings backed by residential mortgages (RMBS, CRT) or commercial real estate (CMBS, mortgage loans) that are subject to the amendment's haircuts and concentration limits.
Compute the phase-in-adjusted haircut for the current step of the 24-month schedule and show both the phased figure and the fully effective 9/30/2026 figure side by side.
Tie the total Available Assets figure to the statutory Annual/Quarterly Statement Schedule D and Exhibit of Assets carrying values and document any bridging item.
Send the classification workbook to the Chief Investment Officer for confirmation that liquidity tiering matches the investment policy and file it against the Section 703 index row.
checklist.done: a quarter-end Available Asset classification workbook exists showing phased and fully effective figures, tied to the statutory statement and confirmed by the Chief Investment Officer.

checklist.step: Refresh the written procedure documents the Enterprise will ask to see
actions: List the procedures PMIERs expects an approved insurer to hold: underwriting and eligibility, quality control, lender approval and monitoring, valuation, claims handling and rescission, servicing oversight, business continuity, and the capital/Available Asset procedure.
For each, check the document has an owner, a version number, an approval date inside the last 12 months and a change log entry for any process change made during the quarter.
Send any procedure older than 12 months back to its owner with a 30-calendar-day re-approval deadline and track it on the readiness gap list.
Publish the approved set to the readiness folder as read-only PDFs stamped with version and approval date so the review copy cannot drift from the live page.
checklist.done: every listed procedure is current within 12 months, versioned, approved and published as a stamped PDF in the readiness folder.

checklist.step: Maintain the standing interview and org roster for an on-site review
actions: Build a roster naming, per PMIERs topic, the person who will be interviewed and their backup: Capital Management Manager (Sections 700-703), Underwriting Quality / Audit Manager (Sections 400-402), Compliance Manager (Sections 600-601), Business Continuity Manager (Section 313), Third-Party Risk Manager (Section 702).
Attach a current org chart for the mortgage guaranty entity showing reporting lines up to the Chief Risk Officer and the Chief Financial Officer.
Record each named person's delegated authority limits and the committee that grants them, drawn from the board-approved delegation of authority.
Refresh the roster within 10 business days of any change in a named role and re-issue it to the Corporate Secretary.
checklist.done: a current roster names a primary and backup interviewee for every PMIERs topic and matches the live org chart.

checklist.step: Run a quarterly call-for-evidence drill against the index
actions: Pick 15 index rows across Sections 402, 600-601 and 700 without warning the owners in advance.
Issue a call-for-evidence to each owner asking for the named artifact as it stood at the quarter-end as-of date, with a 2-business-day return window.
Log receipt time, completeness and whether the artifact is dated on or before the certification it supports.
Raise a readiness gap for every late, incomplete or post-dated item with the owner and a closure date.
checklist.done: all 15 sampled artifacts were requested, timed and assessed, and every failure carries a logged gap with an owner and closure date.

checklist.step: Close readiness gaps before the next Enterprise review window
actions: Open a GRC issue per readiness gap with the PMIERs section, the missing artifact, the cause and the review window it must close before.
Set the target closure date at the earlier of 45 calendar days from raise or 10 business days before the next quarterly submission.
Require the owner to attach the reconstructed artifact to the issue; a written explanation is not closure evidence.
Review the open-gap list with the Head of Compliance monthly and escalate anything aged over 60 calendar days to the Chief Risk Officer.
checklist.done: every readiness gap has a GRC issue, a dated artifact attached at closure, and nothing is open past 60 calendar days without CRO escalation.

checklist.step: Intake and log every Enterprise document request the day it arrives
actions: Record the request in the Enterprise request log the day it is received: Enterprise (Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac), requester name, request date, PMIERs sections cited, items requested and the stated due date.
Compute the internal due date as request date plus 30 calendar days, or the Enterprise's stated date if earlier, and set the task accordingly.
Break each request into numbered sub-items and assign each to the index owner for that section with an internal due date 10 business days ahead of the external one.
Confirm receipt to the Enterprise contact in writing the same week and name the single point of contact for the response.
checklist.done: each request is logged the day it arrives with a computed 30-day due date and numbered sub-items assigned to named owners.

checklist.step: Build the response package and reconcile it to the request items
actions: Assemble responses into a numbered package that mirrors the Enterprise's item numbering one-for-one, with a cover index showing item, response, attachment file name and page count.
Cross-check every figure quoted in the narrative against the source artifact — Exhibit F counts, risk-in-force, Available Assets, Minimum Required Assets — and note the source on the index.
Redact only what the master policy or applicable privacy law requires, and record the redaction basis per item.
Flag any item that cannot be answered fully and draft the partial-response wording for counsel rather than leaving the item blank.
checklist.done: the package answers every numbered item, quotes only figures traced to a named source artifact, and lists any partial response explicitly.

checklist.step: Clear the response through Regulatory Counsel before it leaves the company
actions: Read the full package against the PMIERs sections cited in the request and confirm each answer is responsive rather than adjacent.
Review any statement that concedes a PMIERs non-conformity, a remediation commitment or a date, and rewrite it to be accurate and bounded.
Confirm privilege is preserved where internal audit or legal analysis would otherwise be disclosed, and remove privileged material from the production set.
Sign and date the clearance page; no package is transmitted without it.
checklist.done: counsel has signed and dated the clearance page and every concession or commitment in the package has been reviewed.

checklist.step: Transmit the package and record proof of delivery within the 30-day window
actions: Send the package through the Enterprise's secure transmission channel used for PMIERs reporting and address it to the named counterparty management contact.
Capture the transmission confirmation, timestamp and file manifest and attach them to the request log entry.
Compare the transmission date to the computed 30-calendar-day due date and record days used; anything at 25 days or more triggers a process review.
Close the request log entry only after the Enterprise acknowledges receipt in writing.
checklist.done: the package is transmitted inside 30 calendar days with a stored delivery confirmation and a written Enterprise acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Run a full mock Enterprise review ahead of the April 15 annual certification
actions: Schedule the mock review in February so findings can be cleared before the April 15 annual PMIERs certification.
Issue a realistic document request list covering Sections 313, 402, 600-601 and 700-703 and hold live interviews with the roster's primary names.
Score each topic red / amber / green on evidence completeness, evidence timeliness and interviewee ability to explain the control without notes.
Report red and amber topics to the Head of Compliance and the Chief Financial Officer with owners and dates that land before April 15.
checklist.done: a scored mock review report exists with every red and amber topic owned and dated for closure before April 15.

checklist.step: Archive the readiness file and apply retention
actions: Snapshot the quarter's readiness folder — index, Exhibit F extract, lender and valuation packs, Available Asset workbook, drill results, Enterprise requests and responses — as an immutable quarter-end record.
Apply the retention label of life-of-loan plus 7 years after coverage termination, matching the master policy record-retention terms.
Confirm the repository index makes the snapshot searchable by PMIERs section number, quarter and Enterprise request id.
Record the archive id on the readiness index so a future reviewer can retrieve the quarter as it stood.
checklist.done: the quarter's readiness snapshot is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by PMIERs section, quarter and request id.

testing.step: Build the population of PMIERs evidence obligations and Enterprise requests for the period
actions: Extract every row of the quarter's PMIERs readiness index and every entry in the Enterprise request log for the same period.
Add any PMIERs section referenced in the quarterly submission or the April 15 annual certification that has no index row — omissions are the point of the test.
Reconcile the index row count to the prior quarter's index and explain every added or dropped section against a PMIERs amendment or FAQ.
Sign the population as complete and record the extract date and row counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: the population covers every evidence-bearing PMIERs section plus all Enterprise requests, reconciled to the prior quarter with explained movements.

testing.step: Reconcile the Exhibit F dataset to the source of record
actions: Pull the in-force certificate register at the quarter-end as-of date directly from the policy administration platform, independently of the reporting team's extract.
Compare certificate count, total risk-in-force and delinquency-bucket counts to the filed Exhibit F dataset.
Investigate any variance above 0.1% of risk-in-force to individual certificates and state the cause.
Confirm the same Exhibit F file version was used both for the Enterprise submission and for the Minimum Required Assets calculation.
testing.done: Exhibit F ties to the independent in-force register within 0.1% of risk-in-force with every variance explained, and one file version served both uses.

testing.step: Draw and document the readiness sample
actions: Take 100% of index rows for Sections 402, 600-601 and 703 and 100% of Enterprise requests received in the period.
Take 20 further index rows by seeded random selection from the remaining sections, minimum 35 rows in total.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and selection tool in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Confirm no sampled row is owned by the auditor performing the test.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, covers all Sections 402/600-601/703 rows and all Enterprise requests, and is free of self-review.

testing.step: Re-perform the lender approval judgement on sampled lenders
actions: For each sampled lender open the approval file and independently apply the Sections 600-601 approval criteria: agency seller-servicer standing, licensing, financial condition, QC plan adequacy and executed master policy addendum.
Reach your own approve / decline / monitor conclusion before reading the recorded decision, then compare.

Check the monitoring scorecard for the quarter shows the lender's delinquency, rescission and QC-defect rates against the stated tolerances, and that any breach triggered the action the policy requires.
Treat a correct decision with missing supporting documents as an exception, not a housekeeping note.
testing.done: every sampled lender has an independent re-performance conclusion and a monitoring scorecard with the policy-required action on any tolerance breach.

testing.step: Re-perform the Section 402 valuation and LTV check on sampled certificates
actions: For 25 sampled certificates open the appraisal or waiver record and recompute original LTV = original loan amount ÷ lower of sales price and appraised value.
Compare the recomputed LTV to the LTV carried in the Exhibit F dataset and used in the Minimum Required Assets factor lookup.
Confirm any waiver-based valuation was permitted by the valuation policy version in force on the certificate effective date.
Flag every certificate where an LTV difference would move the loan into a different PMIERs factor band — those change the capital number, not just the file.
testing.done: recomputed LTVs agree with Exhibit F for every sampled certificate, or the band-shifting differences are quantified and logged.

testing.step: Verify the Available Asset classification against the 2024 amendment phase-in
actions: Select the 20 largest holdings plus every holding backed by residential mortgages or commercial real estate and independently assign credit-quality and liquidity tier from the position record.
Recompute the amendment haircut at the correct step of the 24-month phase-in for the quarter tested and compare to the figure in the classification workbook.
Test the concentration limits on RMBS/CMBS-backed holdings and state the headroom or breach in dollars.
Recompute the fully effective 9/30/2026 figure and confirm the capital plan already reflects that end state.
testing.done: sampled holdings are independently classified, phase-in haircuts and concentration limits recompute to the workbook, and the 9/30/2026 end state is reflected in the plan.

testing.step: Trace the evidence trail and identifiers for each sampled index row
actions: Open the artifact named on each sampled index row and confirm it is the version dated on or before the quarter-end as-of date.
Record the artifact's repository id, version, author and approval date in the workpaper.
Confirm the artifact actually supports the PMIERs section claimed — a business continuity plan indexed against Section 601 is a mis-index, not a match.
Time how long each artifact took to retrieve and flag anything over 2 business days.
testing.done: every sampled row resolves to a correctly dated, correctly indexed artifact retrieved within 2 business days, with ids recorded.

testing.step: Recompute the response-deadline maths on every Enterprise request
actions: For each logged Enterprise request recompute the due date as request date plus 30 calendar days and compare to the date used in the task.
Compare the transmission confirmation timestamp to that due date and record days used and days early or late.
Recompute the 45-calendar-day quarterly submission date and the April 15 annual certification date and confirm both were met, using the transmission confirmations as evidence.
Any response transmitted after its computed deadline is a reportable PMIERs breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: every request and periodic submission has a recomputed deadline and a transmission timestamp proving it was met, or a logged breach.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the PMIERs section, the failed attribute (missing, stale, post-dated, mis-indexed, late response) and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause — owner departed, index not refreshed after a PMIERs amendment, artifact stored outside the repository, request intake missed — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date inside 45 calendar days and, for any late Enterprise response, open a self-disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's drill as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date inside 45 days and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the readiness test
actions: Compute the evidence-production pass rate and the on-time response rate and compare both to the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns no indexed artifact and prepared no PMIERs submission, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any open PMIERs breach to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, both rates against threshold, and an Audit Committee reporting date.

In-scope systems.value: Each finding is a GRC issue linked to the owning PMIERs section, the affected control and the remediation evidence; closure artifacts stored in the compliance evidence repository

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Remediation plan back to the Enterprise within 30 calendar days of the finding letter; interim status with the quarterly PMIERs submission at quarter end plus 45 calendar days; all open findings reported in the April 15 annual certification package

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs closure of every high-severity finding and of any finding touching Available Assets, Minimum Required Assets or the sufficiency ratio

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All PMIERs findings open at any point in the period — Enterprise review findings, FHFA examination findings, internal audit findings mapped to a PMIERs section and self-identified breaches — regardless of severity

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly PMIERs remediation test workpaper (population extract, ageing, re-performance notes, exception list) in the compliance evidence repository under Mortgage Guaranty / PMIERs / Remediation

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Remediation log export showing finding id, PMIERs section, severity, root cause, agreed date, actual closure date and closure evidence reference, producible for the Enterprise within 5 business days

checklist.step: Intake the finding and open the remediation record within 5 business days
actions: Log the finding the day the Enterprise or FHFA letter arrives: source (Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, FHFA), letter date, finding id, PMIERs section cited, verbatim finding text and the Enterprise's stated required action and date.

Read the cited PMIERs section yourself — Available Asset standard under the 2024 amendment, Section 402 valuation or Sections 600-601 lender approval — and record whether the citation matches the conduct described.

Assign severity using the finding rating standard: high if it affects Available Assets, Minimum Required Assets or the sufficiency ratio, or if it is a repeat; medium if it affects a PMIERs control without capital effect; low if documentation only.
Name the accountable executive owner from the section index and notify them and the Head of Compliance the same day.
checklist.done: the finding exists as a GRC issue within 5 business days with source, letter date, verified PMIERs citation, severity and a named executive owner.

checklist.step: Scope the finding to the affected population before planning any fix
actions: Translate the finding into a data query — for a valuation finding, all certificates with the affected valuation type in the affected vintages; for a lender finding, all lenders sharing the deficient approval attribute; for an Available Asset finding, all holdings in the affected asset class.
Run the query against the Exhibit F loan-level dataset or the quarter-end position file and record the population count and the risk-in-force or market value exposed.
State explicitly whether the finding is isolated or systemic, using the population count rather than the reviewer's wording.
Send the scoping result to the Capital Management Manager where the population could move Minimum Required Assets or Available Assets.
checklist.done: the finding carries a quantified affected population with counts and exposure, and a written isolated-or-systemic conclusion.

checklist.step: Run a documented root-cause analysis rather than accepting the symptom
actions: Convene the control owner, the process performer and the Compliance Manager and walk the failed control end to end against its written procedure.

Classify the root cause into one of: procedure absent or stale, procedure correct but not followed, system configuration or data defect, judgement error, third-party failure, or PMIERs change not implemented.
Prove the classification with an artifact — the stale procedure version, the system config record, the vendor SLA breach — and attach it to the GRC issue.
Reject 'human error' as a terminal cause; carry it back to the control design that permitted it.
checklist.done: the issue carries one classified root cause supported by a named artifact, with no unqualified 'human error' entries.

checklist.step: Build the remediation plan with dated, owned actions
actions: Split the plan into corrective actions that fix the affected population and preventive actions that stop recurrence, and enter each as its own task with an owner and a date.
Set the overall agreed closure date at or before the Enterprise's required date, with internal task dates at least 10 business days ahead of it.
For each action state the closure evidence that will be produced — a reissued Exhibit F extract, a reclassified position workbook, a re-executed lender approval, an updated procedure version.
Have the accountable executive owner accept the plan in the GRC issue before it is sent anywhere.
checklist.done: the plan has separate corrective and preventive actions, each with an owner, a date inside the agreed date and a named closure artifact, accepted by the executive owner.

checklist.step: Submit the remediation plan to the Enterprise within 30 calendar days
actions: Draft the response letter mirroring the Enterprise's finding numbering, and for each finding state the root cause, the affected population, the corrective and preventive actions and the closure date.
Route the letter to Regulatory Counsel for clearance of any concession or commitment date before transmission.
Send through the Enterprise's secure channel to the named counterparty management contact and capture the transmission confirmation.
Record days used against the 30-calendar-day window on the GRC issue and attach the confirmation.
checklist.done: the plan is transmitted inside 30 calendar days with counsel clearance and a stored delivery confirmation on the issue.

checklist.step: Fix the affected population, not just the process
actions: Work the scoped population case by case — re-underwrite or re-document the affected certificates, re-run the lender approval or re-tier the affected holdings.
Record a per-case disposition: corrected, confirmed correct on review, or unable to correct with a stated reason and the exposure retained.

Where the correction changes loan-level attributes, tell the Regulatory Reporting Analyst so the next Exhibit F submission carries the corrected values and note whether a resubmission of a prior quarter is required.
Report population progress weekly to the executive owner until the count is fully dispositioned.
checklist.done: every case in the scoped population has a recorded disposition and any Exhibit F correction or resubmission need is documented.

checklist.step: Reclassify Available Assets where the finding touches the amended standard
actions: Re-run the Available Asset classification for the affected asset class, applying the amended credit-quality and liquidity tiers and the residential-mortgage and commercial-real-estate limits.
Recompute Available Assets and the sufficiency ratio for the affected quarters at the correct step of the 24-month phase-in and show the before and after figures.
Where the restated ratio changes materially, brief the Chief Financial Officer the same day and confirm whether a corrected quarterly submission is owed to the Enterprise.
Confirm the fully effective 9/30/2026 basis is used in the forward capital plan so the fix is not a one-quarter patch.
checklist.done: affected holdings are reclassified, the sufficiency ratio is restated before and after, and any corrected submission need is decided with the CFO.

checklist.step: Update the procedure, controls and training the root cause pointed at
actions: Amend the written procedure named in the root cause, increment the version and record the change in the document change log with a reference to the finding id.
Have the control owner and the Head of Compliance approve the new version and republish the stamped PDF into the readiness folder.
Where the cause was procedure-not-followed, book targeted training for the named performers and record attendance in the learning management system.
Add or amend the monitoring control that would have caught the failure and record its first execution date.
checklist.done: the procedure is reissued with a version increment referencing the finding, training is recorded, and the new or amended monitoring control has a first execution date.

checklist.step: Request an extension in writing before a date slips, never after
actions: Trigger the extension route as soon as the T-14 reminder shows an action cannot land on the agreed date.
Draft the request stating the reason, the work completed, the revised date and the interim risk mitigation in force until closure.
Get Regulatory Counsel clearance and send to the Enterprise contact before the original date, and record the Enterprise's written agreement on the GRC issue.
Treat a date passed without an agreed extension as a control failure and log it as such, separately from the underlying finding.
checklist.done: no agreed date passes without either closure or a written Enterprise-agreed extension recorded on the issue before the original date.

checklist.step: Prove closure with evidence before changing the status
actions: Collect the closure artifact named in the plan for every action — the reissued extract, restated workbook, re-executed approval file, versioned procedure, training register.
Confirm each artifact is dated on or before the closure date claimed and is stored in the compliance evidence repository with a retrievable id.
Reject narrative-only closure; a status update is not evidence.
Attach the artifact ids to the GRC issue and move the status to Pending independent validation.
checklist.done: every remediation action has a dated closure artifact stored with a repository id and the issue sits at Pending independent validation.

checklist.step: Have the fix independently validated before it is called closed
actions: Re-test the amended control over a fresh sample drawn after the remediation date — never over the same cases the fix team worked.
For population fixes, re-run the original scoping query and confirm the residual count is zero or is explained case by case.
State a validation conclusion of effective, partially effective or not effective, and return partially or not effective issues to the owner with the gap named.
Record the validation sample, date and conclusion on the GRC issue.
checklist.done: each finding has a written validation conclusion from a fresh post-remediation sample, and only effective conclusions may proceed to closure.

checklist.step: Capture executive sign-off on high-severity and capital-affecting closures
actions: Review the root cause, closure evidence and validation conclusion for every high-severity finding and every finding touching Available Assets, Minimum Required Assets or the sufficiency ratio.
Confirm the preventive action, not only the corrective action, is complete and operating.
Sign and date the closure in the GRC issue, or send it back with the specific gap named.
Report closed high-severity findings and any that recurred to the Risk Committee at its next sitting.
checklist.done: no high-severity or capital-affecting finding is closed without a dated CRO signature and a complete preventive action.

checklist.step: Confirm closure with the Enterprise and record their acceptance
actions: Send the closure notification per finding with the evidence summary and the validation conclusion to the Enterprise counterparty management contact.
Track the Enterprise's response and record acceptance, partial acceptance or rejection with the date.
Reopen the GRC issue immediately on rejection, keeping the original finding id and ageing rather than raising a new one.
Keep the internal status as Closed-pending-Enterprise until written acceptance arrives.
checklist.done: each closed finding carries a dated Enterprise acceptance, or is reopened under its original id with continuous ageing.

checklist.step: Report the open-finding position into the quarterly and annual PMIERs cycle
actions: Produce an ageing report at each quarter end showing every open finding by severity, days open, agreed date and days to or past that date.
Include the report in the quarterly PMIERs submission package due within 45 calendar days of quarter end and in the April 15 annual certification package.
Flag every repeat finding explicitly with its prior finding id and prior closure date, since repeats are the Enterprise's sharpest signal.
Present the same report to the Risk Committee with the executive owner named against each item over 90 days old.
checklist.done: an ageing report with repeats flagged is included in the 45-day quarterly package, the April 15 annual package and the Risk Committee pack.

checklist.step: Archive the remediation record and apply retention
actions: Snapshot the closed finding — letter, scoping query and counts, root-cause analysis, plan, correspondence, closure artifacts, validation, sign-offs and Enterprise acceptance — as one immutable record.
Apply 7-year-from-closure retention, extended to life-of-loan plus 7 years where certificate-level corrections were made.
Confirm the record is searchable by finding id, PMIERs section, severity and root-cause class so repeat analysis is possible.
Record the archive id on the GRC issue before it is marked fully closed.
checklist.done: the closed finding is archived as one record, retention-labelled and searchable by finding id, PMIERs section and root-cause class.

testing.step: Build the population of PMIERs findings open or closed in the quarter
actions: Extract every GRC issue tagged PMIERs with a status change, a closure date or an open status inside the quarter, with source, severity, agreed date and actual closure date.
Cross-check the extract against the Enterprise correspondence log and the internal audit finding register so a finding that never reached GRC is caught.
Add self-identified PMIERs breaches reported through the incident and issue routes.
Reconcile the count to the prior quarter's closing open population plus new raises minus closures and explain any residual difference.
testing.done: the population reconciles roll-forward to the prior quarter and includes every finding from correspondence, audit and self-identification.

testing.step: Reconcile the remediation log to the Enterprise correspondence file
actions: Read every Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and FHFA letter received in the period and list each numbered finding it contains.
Match each letter finding to a GRC issue on finding id and PMIERs section; unmatched letter findings are automatic exceptions.
Compare the agreed date in GRC to the required date in the letter and flag any GRC date that is later.
Confirm the severity assigned internally is not lower than the Enterprise's characterisation.
testing.done: every finding in every Enterprise letter matches a GRC issue with a date no later than the letter's and a severity no lower.

testing.step: Draw and document the remediation sample
actions: Take 100% of high-severity findings, 100% of findings touching Available Assets, Minimum Required Assets or the sufficiency ratio, and 100% of repeats.
Take 15 further findings by seeded random selection from the medium and low population, minimum 25 in total.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and tool so the sample is reproducible.
Confirm no sampled finding was owned, executed or validated by the auditor performing this test.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all high-severity, capital-affecting and repeat findings, and is free of self-review.

testing.step: Re-perform the root-cause and scoping judgement on the sample
actions: Read the finding text and the control documentation and reach your own root-cause classification before reading the recorded one, then compare.
Re-run the scoping query against the Exhibit F dataset or the position file for the affected as-of date and compare your population count to the recorded count.
Treat any understated population as an exception — an under-scoped finding cannot be closed, however good the evidence.
Attach both the query used and the count obtained to the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled finding has an independent root cause and population count on file, with any understatement raised as an exception.

testing.step: Re-perform the capital effect on Available Asset findings
actions: For every sampled finding touching the amended Available Asset standard, independently reclassify the affected holdings by credit quality and liquidity tier from the position record.
Recompute Available Assets, Minimum Required Assets and the sufficiency ratio for the affected quarter at the correct phase-in step and compare to the restated figures.
Confirm whether the restated ratio would have crossed 100% and, if so, that the CFO was briefed and a corrected submission was decided on the record.
Recompute the same holdings on the fully effective 9/30/2026 basis and confirm the capital plan reflects it.
testing.done: the sufficiency ratio recomputes to the restated figures for every capital-affecting finding, with the 100% crossing question answered on the record.

testing.step: Trace closure evidence and identifiers for every sampled action
actions: Open the closure artifact named in the plan for each action and confirm it exists, is dated on or before the claimed closure date and carries a repository id.
Confirm the artifact evidences the action described — a training register does not close a system configuration fix.
Check the preventive action has its own artifact separate from the corrective action.
Record artifact id, date and author in the workpaper for each traced action.
testing.done: every sampled action traces to a correctly dated, correctly matched closure artifact with its repository id recorded.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline maths across intake, submission and closure
actions: Recompute intake timeliness as GRC creation date minus letter date and compare to the 5-business-day standard.
Recompute the plan submission deadline as letter date plus 30 calendar days and compare to the transmission confirmation date.
Compare actual closure date to agreed date and, where later, confirm a written Enterprise-agreed extension pre-dates the original date.
Confirm the open-finding ageing report was included in the 45-calendar-day quarterly package and the April 15 annual package.
testing.done: intake, 30-day submission, closure and quarterly/annual reporting dates all recompute as met, or the misses are itemised with day counts.

testing.step: Test whether closed findings actually stayed fixed
actions: For findings closed in the prior two quarters, draw a fresh sample of transactions processed after the closure date through the remediated control.
Re-test the control attribute the finding named and record pass or fail per case.
Any failure is a recurrence: link it to the original finding id, keep the original ageing and raise it as a repeat.
Compare your result to the internal validation conclusion recorded at closure and flag validations that missed a live failure.
testing.done: post-closure re-testing produced a pass rate per finding, and every recurrence is linked to its original finding id and ageing.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the finding id, the failed attribute (late intake, under-scoped, no evidence, missed date without extension, recurrence) and the impact.
Assign a root cause and a named owner at or above the level of the original finding's owner.
Set a remediation date inside 30 calendar days and open a self-disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel for any missed Enterprise-agreed date.
Carry every exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a 30-day date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the remediation test
actions: Compute the on-time closure rate, the evidence-supported closure rate and the recurrence rate and compare each to the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each rate.
Have the independent reviewer, who owned no sampled remediation, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, recurrence rate and any missed Enterprise-agreed dates to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the three rates against threshold, the conclusion and the Audit Committee reporting date.

checklist.step: Refresh the critical process inventory for the mortgage guaranty entity
actions: Open the business continuity module and list every process the entity runs, then mark critical those PMIERs Section 313 names in substance: claims intake, claim adjudication, claim payment, Exhibit F loan-level reporting, the quarterly PMIERs submission, premium billing and investment operations.

For each critical process record the owning department, the process owner by name, the peak volume and the seasonal or period-end peak — quarter end plus 45 days for reporting, month end for claims payment.
Ask the Claims Director / Manager and the Regulatory Reporting Manager to confirm in writing that nothing they own is missing from the critical list.
Retire processes that no longer exist and record the retirement date so the inventory does not silently inflate.
checklist.done: the inventory names every critical process with an owner and peak profile, confirmed in writing by Claims and Regulatory Reporting.

checklist.step: Run the business impact analysis and set RTO and RPO per critical process
actions: For each critical process quantify the impact of outage at 4 hours, 24 hours, 3 days and 7 days across financial loss, Enterprise reporting failure, claimant and servicer harm and reputational effect.

Set the recovery time objective from the point the impact becomes unacceptable, and set the recovery point objective from the maximum tolerable data loss — for claims payment and Exhibit F reporting, state both explicitly in hours.
Anchor the reporting RTO to the hard external dates: the 45-calendar-day quarterly submission, the April 15 annual certification and the 30-calendar-day Enterprise notification window.
Have each process owner sign the BIA record; an unsigned RTO is a proposal, not an objective.
checklist.done: every critical process has a signed BIA with impact by duration and an RTO and RPO in hours tied to the PMIERs external dates.

checklist.step: Map the dependencies behind every critical process
actions: For each critical process pull the supporting configuration items from the CMDB: application, database, integration, hosting location and network path.
Add the non-technology dependencies — the paying bank and payment rail for claim disbursement, the Enterprise secure transmission channel, key vendors, the physical site and the named skilled people.
Mark every dependency with a single point of failure flag where no alternative exists, and quantify what the failure would delay in hours.
Send the dependency map to the IT Service Delivery Manager and the Third-Party Risk Manager for confirmation and record their responses.
checklist.done: each critical process has a confirmed dependency map covering systems, vendors, sites, payment rails and people, with single points of failure flagged.

checklist.step: Document recovery strategies that actually meet the stated RTOs
actions: For each critical system record the recovery strategy — active/active across regions, warm standby with a stated restore time, or backup-and-restore with a stated restore duration.
Compare the strategy's demonstrated recovery time to the process RTO and write the gap in hours where the strategy is slower.
Where a gap exists, either fund the strategy change or raise a formal RTO exception with the Chief Operating Officer — never quietly restate the RTO to match the capability.
Record the backup schedule, retention and last successful restore date for every system supporting claims payment and Exhibit F reporting.
checklist.done: every critical system has a recovery strategy with a demonstrated recovery time compared to its RTO, and each gap has funding or a signed exception.

checklist.step: Write the manual workaround for claims payment and Enterprise reporting
actions: Document how claims continue to be adjudicated and paid with the Claims Platform unavailable: the offline claim register, the authority limits that apply, the payment instruction template and the two-person approval route to Treasury.
Document how the Exhibit F dataset is produced from the last good warehouse snapshot plus a manual delta, who validates it and how it reaches the Enterprise secure channel.
State the maximum duration each workaround can run before backlog becomes unrecoverable, and the trigger for standing up additional resource.
Store the workarounds as printable PDFs available offline, because a plan reachable only through the failed network is not a plan.
checklist.done: offline claims-payment and Exhibit F workarounds exist as offline-available documents with authority limits, validation steps and a stated maximum run duration.

checklist.step: Name recovery teams, contacts and delegated authorities
actions: Build the recovery roster per critical process with a primary and at least one deputy, their mobile numbers and their out-of-band contact method.
Validate every name against the HRIS active-employee list and remove leavers within 5 business days of their exit date.
Record the delegated authority that applies in a disruption — claim payment approval limits, the authority to notify the Enterprise, the authority to declare an invocation.
Distribute the roster as a wallet card and an offline PDF, and re-issue it quarterly.
checklist.done: the roster names primary and deputy for each critical process, is validated against HRIS with no leavers, and states disruption-time authority limits.

checklist.step: Write the invocation, escalation and Enterprise notification steps
actions: Define the invocation criteria in measurable terms — claims payment unavailable beyond 4 hours, Exhibit F pipeline unavailable inside the 45-day submission window, site inaccessible beyond one business day.
Name who may declare an invocation and their deputy, and the crisis bridge details.

Write the Enterprise notification step into the plan: who drafts, who clears with Regulatory Counsel and the 30-calendar-day outer limit for notifying Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac of a material operational event.
Include the template notification with placeholders for event, impacted PMIERs obligations, containment status and expected restoration.
checklist.done: the plan states measurable invocation triggers, named declaring authority, and an Enterprise notification step with a template and the 30-day limit.

checklist.step: Fold vendor and outsourced dependencies into the plan
actions: List the vendors supporting critical processes — claims administration support, servicing data providers, the payment processor, the hosting provider and any third-party risk analytics firm engaged under Section 702.
Pull each contract and record the contracted availability, recovery commitments, notification obligations and audit or exercise rights.
Obtain each vendor's current continuity plan summary and last exercise result, and record the date received.
Raise a gap where a critical vendor's recovery commitment is slower than the process RTO it supports, and record the interim mitigation.
checklist.done: every critical vendor has contracted recovery terms, a dated continuity summary on file and either RTO alignment or a logged gap with mitigation.

checklist.step: Re-approve the plan annually before the April 15 certification
actions: Review the refreshed inventory, BIA, RTO/RPO table, dependency map, workarounds, roster and open gap register as one package.
Challenge every RTO exception and every open single point of failure and record the decision to accept, fund or escalate.
Sign and date the approval page, increment the plan version and note the approval to the board Risk Committee.
Complete approval before April 1 so the approved plan can be cited in the April 15 annual PMIERs certification.
checklist.done: a signed, dated, version-incremented approval page exists before April 1 with every RTO exception and single point of failure explicitly decided.

checklist.step: Publish and distribute the approved plan so it is usable under failure
actions: Publish the approved version to the document management repository with version, approval date and approver on the cover page, and archive the superseded version rather than overwriting it.
Distribute offline copies — printed and locally stored PDFs — to every roster member and to the alternate site.
Record distribution acknowledgements per roster member and chase non-acknowledgements within 10 business days.
Publish a one-page quick reference with invocation triggers, bridge details and the first six actions.
checklist.done: the approved version is published, the prior version archived, offline copies distributed and acknowledgements recorded for every roster member.

checklist.step: Trigger an out-of-cycle plan update on any material change
actions: Configure the change process so any change touching a Section 313 critical system, site, vendor or process owner raises a BCP impact task on the Business Continuity Manager.
Require the change record to state whether the RTO, RPO, dependency map or roster is affected before the change can close.
Hold the change in a pending state until the plan section is updated or the Business Continuity Manager records that no update is needed with a reason.
Report monthly on changes closed with an unresolved BCP impact task.
checklist.done: no change to a critical system, site, vendor or owner closes without a recorded BCP impact assessment.

checklist.step: Train the roster on their plan role
actions: Deliver role-specific briefings: claims teams on the offline claim register and payment authority, reporting teams on the manual Exhibit F path, executives on invocation and Enterprise notification.
Run a tabletop walkthrough of the claims-payment workaround with the actual performers, not their managers.
Record attendance and completion in the learning management system and chase non-completion within 20 business days.
Capture questions raised in training as candidate plan clarifications and feed them into the next version.
checklist.done: every roster member has completed role-specific training recorded in the LMS, and training questions are logged as plan feedback.

checklist.step: Maintain the resilience gap register and drive it down
actions: Log every RTO shortfall, unmitigated single point of failure, stale BIA and vendor misalignment as a GRC issue with the affected critical process named.
Set closure dates and record the interim mitigation that holds the risk until closure — a mitigation is required even where the fix is a year out.
Review the register monthly with the Chief Operating Officer and quarterly with the Risk Committee.
Escalate to the Chief Risk Officer any gap affecting claims payment or Exhibit F reporting that is open beyond 90 calendar days.
checklist.done: every resilience gap is logged with an interim mitigation and a closure date, and claims/reporting gaps over 90 days are escalated to the CRO.

checklist.step: Assemble the Section 313 evidence pack for the Enterprise
actions: Collate the approved plan with its signed approval page, the BIA summary, the RTO/RPO table, the dependency map, the latest exercise results and the gap register.
Add a Section 313 cross-reference sheet mapping each PMIERs expectation to the plan page that satisfies it.
File the pack against the Section 313 row of the PMIERs readiness index and note the version and date.
Confirm the pack can be produced in full within 5 business days of an Enterprise request.
checklist.done: a Section 313 pack with a cross-reference sheet is filed against the readiness index and producible within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Archive superseded plan versions under retention
actions: Move each superseded plan version, with its approval page and supporting BIA, into the retention-managed archive on publication of a new version.
Apply 7-year retention from supersession so the plan in force on any past date can be reproduced for an Enterprise review.
Index by version, approval date and effective period and confirm retrievability by date range.
Record the archive id on the plan register.
checklist.done: every superseded version is archived with its approval page, retention-labelled and retrievable by effective date.

testing.step: Build the population of critical processes and plan components
actions: Extract the critical process inventory with owner, BIA date, RTO, RPO, dependency map date and roster date as at the test date.
Add every process that appears in the claims, reporting or investment operations org charts but not in the inventory — omission is a primary failure mode.
Reconcile the inventory to the prior year and explain every addition and retirement.
Sign the population as complete and record extract date and counts.
testing.done: the population covers every critical process, reconciles to the prior year with explained movements, and is signed complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the plan's system list to the CMDB and the reporting pipeline
actions: Pull the CMDB configuration items supporting the Claims Platform, Policy Administration Platform and the Exhibit F reporting pipeline, including databases, integrations and hosting locations.
Compare against the dependency maps in the plan and list systems present in the CMDB but absent from the plan, and vice versa.
Confirm the criticality rating in the CMDB matches the plan's classification for each system.
Investigate every mismatch to a named cause rather than reconciling it away.
testing.done: the plan's dependency maps reconcile item by item to the CMDB, with every mismatch explained by a named cause.

testing.step: Draw and document the plan-component sample
actions: Take 100% of processes touching claims payment and Exhibit F reporting and 100% of processes with an open RTO exception.
Take 8 further critical processes by seeded random selection, minimum 15 in total.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and tool for reproducibility.
Confirm no sampled component was authored by the reviewer performing the test.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all claims-payment, Exhibit F and RTO-exception processes, and is free of self-review.

testing.step: Re-perform the BIA judgement and RTO derivation on the sample
actions: For each sampled process derive your own impact-by-duration assessment from volumes, external deadlines and claimant effect before reading the recorded BIA.
Compare your RTO to the recorded RTO and treat any recorded RTO longer than the point of unacceptable impact as an exception.
Confirm the reporting RTO is short enough to preserve the 45-calendar-day quarterly submission and the April 15 annual certification from a realistic worst-case invocation date.
Confirm every BIA carries a process-owner signature dated within 12 months.
testing.done: each sampled process has an independently derived RTO compared to the recorded one, and every BIA is owner-signed within 12 months.

testing.step: Test the recovery strategy against the stated RTO for sampled systems
actions: For each sampled critical system read the documented recovery strategy and the most recent evidenced recovery time from a real restore or failover.
Compare demonstrated recovery time to the process RTO and record the gap in hours.
Verify the last successful restore date for the underlying data and that the restore covered the RPO window claimed.
Treat any RTO supported only by design intent, with no evidenced recovery, as unsupported.
testing.done: every sampled system's RTO is either evidenced by a real recovery within the objective or recorded as unsupported with the gap in hours.

testing.step: Test contact, roster and authority currency
actions: Match every roster name to the HRIS active-employee list and flag leavers and role changes since the last roster issue.
Send an out-of-band contact test to 20 roster members and record response within 60 minutes.
Confirm the recorded disruption-time authority limits match the current delegation of authority approved by the board.
Flag any critical process whose primary and deputy are both unreachable or both in the same location.
testing.done: the roster contains no leavers, contact response is recorded for the tested members, and no critical process has both named recoverers unreachable or co-located.

testing.step: Trace the plan evidence and version identifiers
actions: Open the current approved plan and confirm the approval page carries the Chief Operating Officer signature, a date and a version number.
Confirm the version in the repository matches the version distributed offline to the roster and to the alternate site.
Confirm superseded versions are archived and retrievable for any past date within the 7-year retention window.
Record document ids, versions and approval dates in the workpaper.
testing.done: the approved, distributed and archived versions agree, with signature, date and version recorded in the workpaper.

testing.step: Recompute the annual review and notification deadline maths
actions: Compare the plan approval date to the April 1 internal milestone and the April 15 annual PMIERs certification date and record days early or late.
Compute the elapsed months since the last BIA refresh for each critical process and flag anything over 12 months.
Model a disruption starting on the worst-case date inside the quarterly cycle and confirm the documented recovery path still delivers the submission within 45 calendar days of quarter end.
Confirm the plan's Enterprise notification step is bounded by 30 calendar days and names who clears it.
testing.done: approval timing, BIA ages and the modelled 45-day submission path are all recomputed and stated, with the 30-day notification bound confirmed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the critical process, the failed attribute (stale BIA, unsupported RTO, missing dependency, leaver on roster, unapproved plan) and the resilience impact.
Assign a root cause — change not routed to BCP, owner turnover, vendor term never negotiated, exercise never run — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and require an interim mitigation for anything affecting claims payment or Exhibit F reporting.
Carry every open exception into the next annual assurance as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and an interim mitigation where claims or reporting are affected.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the Section 313 plan assurance
actions: Compute the share of critical processes with a current BIA, a supported RTO and a clean roster and compare each to the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — citing the workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored no part of the plan, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Risk Committee before April 15 so the conclusion informs the annual PMIERs certification, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the three coverage rates, the conclusion and a Risk Committee reporting date before April 15.
