Pass/fail thresholds.value: Fail if a critical system has no completed exercise in the trailing 12 months, if the achieved recovery time exceeded the RTO, if data restored missed the RPO window, or if the exercise was scoped so narrowly it never exercised the failure; any Claims Platform or Exhibit F failure escalates to the Chief Operating Officer

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual per critical system; the assurance test runs annually in Q1 over the trailing 12 months of exercises, with a quarterly check that the exercise calendar is on track

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have executed, scripted or observed the exercise being assessed and must not sit in the recovery engineering team

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual resilience exercise assurance workpaper (exercise inventory, timestamped run logs, RTO/RPO achieved versus objective, defect ageing) in the compliance evidence repository under Mortgage Guaranty / PMIERs / Section 313 / Exercises

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-system exercise report with scenario, participants, start and recovery timestamps, achieved RTO and RPO against objective, defects raised and closure status, producible for the Enterprise within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: IT Operations supplies exercise evidence to Market Conduct Compliance, who is the single channel to the Enterprise; the Chief Information Officer approves any statement about demonstrated recovery capability before it is sent

checklist.step: Build the annual exercise calendar from the critical system list
actions: Take the Section 313 critical system list from the Business Continuity Manager and create one exercise record per system for the calendar year.
Schedule the Claims Platform and Exhibit F pipeline exercises in Q3 or Q4 so defects can be remediated and retested before the April 15 annual certification.
Avoid the quarter-end plus 45-day reporting window and month-end claims payment peaks when placing exercise dates, and record the reasoning.
Publish the calendar to the Chief Information Officer, the Claims Director / Manager and the Regulatory Reporting Manager for date acceptance.
checklist.done: every critical system has a dated exercise record for the year, cleared of reporting and payment peaks and accepted by the business owners.

checklist.step: Design the scenario so it exercises a real failure, not a rehearsal
actions: Choose a scenario from the risk profile — region loss, ransomware-driven isolation of the production estate, database corruption requiring point-in-time restore, or loss of the Enterprise transmission channel.
Write the scenario script with the injected failure, what participants are and are not told, and the decision points that must be reached.
State explicitly what is out of scope and why, so the report cannot later imply coverage the exercise never had.
Have the Business Continuity Manager confirm the scenario maps to a documented plan section and to the process RTO being claimed.
checklist.done: the scenario script names the injected failure, the decision points, the explicit out-of-scope items and the plan section it exercises.

checklist.step: Set entry criteria and freeze the environment before execution
actions: Raise the change record for the exercise window with rollback plan, blast radius and the named abort authority.
Confirm entry criteria: current backups verified, recovery runbooks at the current version, participants confirmed, monitoring and timestamping in place.
Freeze non-exercise changes to the systems in scope for the exercise window and notify the service desk.
Confirm the production claims payment and reporting paths are protected or that the exercise is genuinely running in production with executive approval on record.
checklist.done: an approved change record exists with entry criteria met, a change freeze in force and a named abort authority.

checklist.step: Execute the failover or restore and timestamp every milestone
actions: Record the wall-clock timestamp of failure injection, detection, declaration, recovery start, service restored and full verification, in a run log kept as the exercise executes.
Follow the published runbook exactly and log every deviation, including undocumented steps the engineers knew but the runbook did not.
Capture the restore point actually achieved — the last committed transaction recovered — not the backup timestamp.
Do not stop the clock at technical availability; stop it when a business user completes a real transaction.
checklist.done: a timestamped run log exists from injection to verified business transaction, with every runbook deviation recorded.

checklist.step: Prove the recovered Claims Platform can actually pay a claim
actions: In the recovered environment open a test claim on an insured certificate and take it through intake, adjudication, approval within authority limits and payment instruction generation.
Confirm the claim history, servicer data and master policy terms recovered intact by comparing a sample of five claims to their pre-failure state.
Confirm the payment file reaches Treasury in the expected format and that the two-person approval control still enforces.
Record the elapsed time from service restored to first successful end-to-end claim as the business recovery time.
checklist.done: an end-to-end test claim completed in the recovered environment with intact history and an enforced approval control, and business recovery time is recorded.

checklist.step: Prove the Exhibit F reporting pipeline can still produce a submission
actions: In the recovered environment re-run the Exhibit F extract for the last completed quarter-end as-of date.
Compare row count, total risk-in-force and delinquency-bucket counts to the previously submitted file and confirm they match exactly.
Confirm the Enterprise secure transmission path can be reached from the recovered environment using a test transmission, without sending real data to Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac.
Record whether the recovered pipeline could deliver inside the 45-calendar-day submission window from a worst-case invocation date.
checklist.done: the recovered pipeline reproduces the last submitted Exhibit F exactly, the transmission path is proven reachable, and the 45-day feasibility is stated.

checklist.step: Prove the investment position feed behind Available Assets recovers
actions: Re-run the quarter-end position extract in the recovered environment and compare CUSIP count, market value and NAIC designation fields to the previously used file.
Confirm the credit-quality and liquidity tier attributes needed for the amended Available Asset classification survived the restore.
Recompute total Available Assets from the recovered feed and compare to the figure used in the last submission.
Report any attribute loss to the Capital Management Manager the same day, since a missing tier attribute silently changes the sufficiency ratio.
checklist.done: the recovered position feed reproduces the prior quarter's Available Assets figure with all classification attributes intact, or the loss is reported to Capital Management.

checklist.step: Run the tabletop for the manual workarounds alongside the technical test
actions: Walk the actual claims and reporting performers through the offline claim register, the payment authority limits and the manual Exhibit F build with systems declared unavailable.
Time how long the group takes to reach the first payable claim and the first validated dataset using paper and offline copies only.
Record whether participants could locate the offline plan copy without network access — an unfound plan is a failed control.
Capture every question that the plan could not answer as a defect against the plan, not against the participants.
checklist.done: the tabletop produced timed manual outcomes, confirmed offline plan availability, and logged every unanswered question as a plan defect.

checklist.step: Measure achieved RTO and RPO against the objectives and state the gap
actions: Compute achieved RTO as declaration timestamp to first successful business transaction, and achieved RPO as the gap between the last committed pre-failure transaction and the earliest recovered one.
Compare both to the BIA objectives for each affected process and record the gap in hours, positive or negative.
Where the objective was missed, state whether the cause was capability, runbook quality or decision latency, because the fixes differ.
Send every missed objective to the Business Continuity Manager for the resilience gap register the same week.
checklist.done: achieved RTO and RPO are computed from the run log, compared to objective in hours, and every miss is classified and handed to the gap register.

checklist.step: Raise, rate and route every exercise defect
actions: Raise a defect per issue observed — runbook step wrong or missing, dependency not recovered, credential or certificate expired, monitoring blind, capacity short at the recovery site.
Rate critical any defect that would have prevented claim payment or Exhibit F production in a real event; rate the rest major or minor.
Assign each defect an owner and a fix date, with critical defects due inside 45 calendar days.
Link every defect to the exercise record so the retest scope is unambiguous.
checklist.done: every observation is a rated, owned, dated defect linked to its exercise record, with critical defects due inside 45 calendar days.

checklist.step: Correct the runbooks and the plan from what the exercise revealed
actions: Rewrite every runbook step that was wrong, ambiguous or missing, including the undocumented steps engineers performed from memory.
Increment the runbook version and record the exercise id in the change log so the correction is traceable to its cause.
Feed dependency, contact and authority corrections to the Business Continuity Manager for the plan update.
Have a second engineer who did not run the exercise read the revised runbook and confirm it is executable as written.
checklist.done: runbooks are reissued with version increments citing the exercise id and confirmed executable by an engineer who did not run the exercise.

checklist.step: Retest critical defects rather than closing them on assertion
actions: Schedule a targeted retest for every critical defect within 45 calendar days of the exercise.
Re-execute only the failed segment — the failed restore step, the unreachable dependency, the expired certificate path — with timestamps.
Record the retest result on the defect and close only on a passing retest with evidence.
Escalate any critical defect still open at 45 calendar days to the Chief Information Officer and the Chief Operating Officer.
checklist.done: every critical defect has a timestamped passing retest or a documented escalation at the 45-day mark.

checklist.step: Write and sign the post-exercise report
actions: Write the report with scenario, scope and explicit exclusions, participants, the timestamped milestone table, achieved versus objective RTO and RPO, defects by severity and the retest plan.
Attach the run log, the business verification evidence from Claims and Reporting and the restore verification output.
Have the Chief Information Officer and the Business Continuity Manager sign the report.
File it in the compliance evidence repository against the Section 313 readiness index row.
checklist.done: a signed post-exercise report with timestamps, achieved-versus-objective figures and attached verification evidence is filed against the Section 313 index row.

checklist.step: Report the annual exercise position into the PMIERs certification pack
actions: Produce a one-page annual position showing, per critical system, the last exercise date, scenario, achieved RTO and RPO against objective and open critical defects.
Include it in the April 15 annual PMIERs certification pack and in the quarterly submission package as a status update.
Flag any critical system with no exercise in the trailing 12 months in red with a committed date.
Present the same page to the Risk Committee with the Chief Information Officer speaking to any red line.
checklist.done: the annual exercise position is in the April 15 certification pack and the Risk Committee pack, with unexercised systems flagged and dated.

checklist.step: Archive exercise evidence under retention
actions: Snapshot each exercise — scenario script, change record, run log, verification evidence, defects and signed report — as one immutable record.
Apply 7-year retention so a prior year's demonstrated recovery time can be evidenced to the Enterprise.
Index by system, exercise date, scenario type and achieved RTO so trend questions can be answered without reopening files.
Record the archive id on the exercise record before it is closed.
checklist.done: each exercise is archived as one retention-labelled record, indexed by system, date, scenario and achieved RTO.

testing.step: Build the population of required and completed exercises
actions: Extract every exercise record with system, scheduled date, executed date, scenario, status and defect count for the trailing 12 months.
Join to the Section 313 critical system list so systems with no exercise record appear in the population as nulls rather than being absent.
Add tabletop exercises of the manual claims-payment and Exhibit F workarounds.
Sign the population as complete and record extract date, system count and exercise count.
testing.done: the population lists every critical system with its exercise or an explicit null, plus the workaround tabletops, and is signed complete.

testing.step: Reconcile exercise coverage to the plan's critical system list and the CMDB
actions: Compare the exercised system list to the CMDB configuration items flagged critical for the mortgage guaranty entity.
List critical systems never exercised and systems exercised but not classified critical, and explain both.
Confirm each exercised system's scope covered its dependent databases and integrations, not the application tier alone.
Escalate any unexercised Claims Platform or Exhibit F component immediately rather than at report time.
testing.done: coverage reconciles system by system to the CMDB critical list, with unexercised critical components escalated on discovery.

testing.step: Draw and document the exercise sample
actions: Take 100% of exercises covering the Claims Platform, the Exhibit F pipeline and the investment position feed.
Take 5 further exercises by seeded random selection, minimum 10 in total, and include every exercise that was aborted or rescheduled.
Record seed, population size, selection date and tool for reproducibility.
Confirm the reviewer executed, scripted or observed none of the sampled exercises.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all claims, reporting and investment exercises plus aborts, and is free of self-review.

testing.step: Re-perform the RTO and RPO measurement from the raw run log
actions: Take the raw timestamped run log for each sampled exercise and independently compute achieved RTO from declaration to first successful business transaction.
Independently compute achieved RPO from the last pre-failure committed transaction to the earliest recovered transaction, using the database evidence rather than the backup schedule.
Compare both to the reported figures and treat any clock stopped at technical availability rather than business transaction as an overstatement exception.
Compare achieved figures to the BIA objectives and record the gap in hours.
testing.done: each sampled exercise has independently recomputed RTO and RPO compared to both the reported figures and the BIA objectives.

testing.step: Verify the business verification actually happened
actions: For claims exercises open the test claim referenced in the report and confirm it exists with intake, adjudication, approval and payment instruction steps completed in the recovered environment.
For reporting exercises open the regenerated Exhibit F output and compare row count and total risk-in-force to the previously submitted file, byte-level where possible.
Confirm the business verifier named in the report is from Claims or Regulatory Reporting and not from the recovery team.
Treat a report claiming business verification with no verifier-side artifact as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled exercise's business verification is evidenced by a real recovered-environment artifact signed off by a business-side verifier.

testing.step: Test whether the scenario genuinely exercised the failure
actions: Read the scenario script and the run log together and confirm the failure was injected rather than simulated by announcement.
Confirm the recovery ran from the recovery capability under test rather than falling back to the production instance mid-exercise.
Check the stated out-of-scope list against the RTO being claimed and flag any claim that rests on an untested segment.
Flag any exercise where participants were pre-briefed on the exact injection as coverage-limited.
testing.done: each sampled exercise is confirmed as a genuine injected failure recovered by the capability under test, or its coverage limitation is stated.

testing.step: Trace defects, retests and evidence identifiers
actions: For each sampled exercise list every defect raised with severity, owner, due date and status, and confirm each links back to the exercise record.
For every critical defect confirm a timestamped passing retest exists and pre-dates the closure date.
Confirm runbook versions were incremented after the exercise and the change log cites the exercise id.
Record defect ids, retest dates and runbook versions in the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled defect traces to an owner, a due date and — for criticals — a timestamped passing retest, with runbook versions recorded.

testing.step: Recompute the annual coverage and defect-clock maths
actions: For each critical system compute months since the last completed exercise as at April 15 and flag anything over 12.
Recompute each critical defect's age as closure date minus exercise date and compare to the 45-calendar-day standard.
Confirm every exercise completed before April 15 is reflected in the annual PMIERs certification pack and that none was reported before it completed.
Confirm no exercise was scheduled inside the quarter-end plus 45-day reporting window without documented approval.
testing.done: coverage ages, defect ages and certification-pack inclusion are all recomputed and stated against their standards.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the system, the failed attribute (no exercise, RTO missed, RPO missed, no business verification, critical defect open past 45 days) and the resilience impact.
Assign a root cause — capacity at the recovery site, runbook decay, scheduling conflict with reporting peaks, ownership vacancy — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and require an interim mitigation for any claims-payment or Exhibit F exposure.
Carry every exception into the next annual assurance as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and an interim mitigation where claims or reporting are exposed.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the resilience testing assurance
actions: Compute the share of critical systems exercised in the trailing 12 months, the share meeting RTO and the share meeting RPO, and compare each to threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each rate.
Have the independent reviewer, who ran no sampled exercise, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Risk Committee before April 15 so the conclusion informs the annual PMIERs certification, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states coverage, RTO and RPO rates against threshold, the conclusion and a Risk Committee date before April 15.

checklist.step: Rebuild the third-party inventory from spend, not from memory
actions: Export every supplier with purchase orders or invoices paid in the last 12 months for the mortgage guaranty entity, with legal entity name, spend, cost centre and the requisitioner.
Reconcile the supplier list to the third-party register and list suppliers paid but not registered, and registered suppliers with no spend.
Chase each unregistered supplier's requisitioner for the service description and business owner within 10 business days.
Retire dormant register entries with a recorded termination date rather than deleting them.
checklist.done: the register reconciles to 12 months of AP spend with every unregistered paid supplier chased and every dormant entry dated as terminated.

checklist.step: Tier every third party by criticality against PMIERs impact
actions: Score each third party on whether its failure would stop claim payment, stop Exhibit F reporting, corrupt loan-level or valuation data, or impair the Available Asset calculation.
Assign tier: critical, ICT-critical, important or standard, and record the specific PMIERs section its failure would breach.
Tier the Section 702 risk analytics firm as critical by definition, because its opinion feeds the Enterprise's view of the capital position.
Have each business owner confirm the tier in writing; disputes go to the Operational Risk Manager, not to the vendor.
checklist.done: every third party carries a written-confirmed tier and the named PMIERs section its failure would breach.

checklist.step: Run tier-appropriate due diligence before and after onboarding
actions: For critical and ICT-critical vendors collect the current SOC 1 Type II or SOC 2 Type II report, financial statements, insurance certificates, continuity plan summary, subcontractor list and information-security questionnaire.
Read the SOC report's complementary user entity controls and record which of them this company is actually performing, with the owner named.
Record every qualified opinion or exception in the SOC report as a diligence finding with a mitigation, rather than filing the report unread.
Set the diligence expiry to 12 months from the report period end for critical tiers and load the expiry into the register.
checklist.done: every critical and ICT-critical vendor has a complete, read diligence pack with CUEC ownership assigned and a dated 12-month expiry in the register.

checklist.step: Put the PMIERs-required terms into the contract before signature
actions: Check each critical contract for the mandatory clauses: audit and inspection rights extending to the Enterprises and FHFA, record retention aligned to life-of-loan plus 7 years, incident notification inside 24 hours, service levels matching the process RTO, subcontracting consent, data location and return-or-destruction on exit.
Record clause-by-clause presence in the CLM metadata so the register can report gaps without reopening the PDF.
Route missing clauses to General Counsel for a contract amendment with a target date, and record the interim mitigation until it is executed.
Block signature of any new critical contract missing an audit-rights or incident-notification clause.
checklist.done: every critical contract has clause-level metadata in the CLM, with each missing clause under an amendment with a target date and an interim mitigation.

checklist.step: Engage the Section 702 risk analytics firm when the Enterprise requires it
actions: On receipt of an Enterprise request under Section 702, record the requesting Enterprise, the scope of opinion sought and the firm the Enterprise has selected.
Open the engagement within 30 calendar days: confirm the firm's independence, agree the scope letter, and confirm the insurer bears the cost as Section 702 requires.
Give the firm a controlled data package — Exhibit F loan-level dataset, position file, reserving and capital model outputs — logged item by item with the date supplied.
Route the engagement letter through General Counsel and record Chief Risk Officer approval before work starts.
checklist.done: the Section 702 engagement is opened inside 30 calendar days with a scope letter, an itemised data log, counsel review and CRO approval.

checklist.step: Receive, challenge and act on the Section 702 opinion
actions: Review the delivered opinion with the Capital Management Manager and the Chief Actuary, focusing on any difference from the company's own risk and capital view.
Record management's response to each finding — accept, accept with mitigation, or challenge with evidence — before the opinion is discussed with the Enterprise.
Where the opinion implies a change to Available Assets, Minimum Required Assets or the sufficiency ratio, task Capital Management to quantify it the same week.
Report the opinion and management's response to the Risk Committee and file both against the Section 702 readiness index row.
checklist.done: the opinion carries a documented management response per finding, a quantified capital effect where implied, and a Risk Committee reporting date.

checklist.step: Maintain the ICT and data-flow view of critical vendors
actions: For each ICT-critical vendor record the systems it hosts or connects to, the integration method, the data categories exchanged and the direction of flow.
Flag every flow carrying borrower personal data, loan-level data used for Exhibit F, or investment position data used for Available Assets.
Record hosting country and any subcontracted processing location for each flow.
Reconcile this view to the plan's dependency maps so the register and the continuity plan cannot disagree.
checklist.done: every ICT-critical vendor has a documented data-flow record reconciled to the continuity plan dependency maps.

checklist.step: Monitor critical vendors on a fixed cadence against contracted terms
actions: Hold quarterly service reviews with critical vendors and record availability, incident count, SLA credits, open defects and any change to subcontractors or key personnel.
Track financial-health signals — rating changes, going-concern language, ownership change — and record the source and date.
Compare actual service levels to the contracted levels and to the process RTO they support, and raise a gap where they diverge.
File each review with the vendor's register entry and update the last-monitored date.
checklist.done: every critical vendor has a dated quarterly review on file with SLA performance compared to contract and to the supported RTO.

checklist.step: Analyse concentration and substitutability across the register
actions: Group critical vendors by service, by underlying cloud or hosting provider and by ultimate parent to reveal hidden common dependencies.
Identify services where a single vendor supports more than one critical process and quantify what its failure would stop.
Score substitutability — time to replace, availability of alternatives, data portability — and mark any vendor with no viable substitute.
Report concentration findings to the Chief Risk Officer quarterly with a mitigation for each unsubstitutable critical vendor.
checklist.done: a quarterly concentration analysis names common dependencies and unsubstitutable critical vendors, each with a recorded mitigation.

checklist.step: Hold an exit plan for every critical vendor
actions: Write an exit plan per critical vendor covering trigger events, the alternative provider or in-house route, data extraction format and timetable, and the transition run cost.
Confirm the contract's return-or-destruction and transition-assistance terms actually support the plan, and amend where they do not.
State the elapsed time to exit and compare it to the RTO of the processes the vendor supports.
Review each exit plan annually and after any material change in the vendor's ownership or service.
checklist.done: every critical vendor has a dated exit plan with an elapsed-time-to-exit figure compared to the supported process RTO.

checklist.step: Route vendor incidents into the company incident process
actions: Register the vendor's contractual notification contact and the 24-hour notification requirement in the vendor record.
On any vendor incident notification, open an incident record the same day with the affected process, data categories and PMIERs impact assessment.
Notify the Operational Risk Manager immediately where claims payment, Exhibit F reporting or borrower data is affected, so the Enterprise notification clock can be assessed.
Track the vendor's root-cause report and corrective actions to closure in the vendor record.
checklist.done: every vendor incident notification produces a same-day internal incident record with a PMIERs impact assessment and tracked vendor corrective actions.

checklist.step: Attest the register quarterly with named business owners
actions: Issue each business owner their vendor rows at quarter end plus 10 business days and require confirmation of tier, service description, contract currency and continued need.
Require owners to flag services that have changed scope or moved to a subcontractor since the last attestation.
Chase non-responders at 5 and 10 business days and escalate to their department head after 15.
Record the attestation date and attester name on each register row so the register carries provenance.
checklist.done: every register row carries a dated quarterly attestation from its named business owner, with escalations recorded for non-responders.

checklist.step: Clear third-party exceptions to closure
actions: Log expired diligence, missing clauses, unattested rows, unregistered paid suppliers and unsubstitutable critical vendors as GRC issues with the affected PMIERs section named.
Set closure dates and record the interim mitigation holding the risk — increased monitoring, restricted data flow, held payment — until closure.
Require Chief Risk Officer acceptance in writing for any critical vendor continuing to operate with an open gap beyond 60 calendar days.
Review the exception list with the Procurement Manager monthly.
checklist.done: every third-party exception has an issue, an interim mitigation, a closure date and, past 60 days, written CRO acceptance.

checklist.step: Package the third-party evidence for the Enterprise
actions: Export the register with tier, service, business owner, diligence date, clause status, last monitoring date, concentration flag and exit-plan date.
Add the Section 702 engagement letter, the delivered opinion and management's documented response.
Attach the concentration analysis and the exception list with mitigations.
File the pack against the Section 702 readiness index row and confirm it can be produced within 5 business days.
checklist.done: a third-party pack including the Section 702 opinion and management response is filed against the readiness index and producible within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Archive register snapshots and vendor files under retention
actions: Snapshot the register at each quarter end as an immutable record so the population as at any past quarter can be reproduced.
On termination, archive the vendor file — contract, diligence, monitoring, incidents, exit execution — as one record.
Apply 7-year-from-termination retention and index by vendor legal entity, tier and service.
Record the archive id on the register row before it is retired.
checklist.done: quarter-end register snapshots and terminated vendor files are archived, retention-labelled and indexed by entity, tier and service.

testing.step: Build the third-party population from register and spend together
actions: Extract every supplier paid by the mortgage guaranty entity in the period from the general ledger with legal entity, spend and cost centre.
Extract the third-party register with tier, owner, diligence date, clause status and attestation date.
Outer-join the two so paid-but-unregistered and registered-but-unpaid entries both appear, and count each group.
Sign the population as complete and record extract dates, supplier count and register count.
testing.done: the population is the outer join of GL spend and the register, with both mismatch groups counted, signed complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to the source of record for critical services
actions: Compare ICT-critical register entries to the CMDB's externally hosted or externally integrated configuration items.
Compare critical register entries to the continuity plan's vendor dependency lists and to the Section 702 engagement record.
List vendors present in one source and absent from another and drive each to a named cause.
Confirm every vendor touching Exhibit F data, valuation data or investment positions is registered as critical or ICT-critical.
testing.done: the register reconciles to the CMDB, the continuity plan and the Section 702 record, with every difference explained.

testing.step: Draw and document the vendor sample
actions: Take 100% of critical and ICT-critical vendors, 100% of paid-but-unregistered suppliers and the Section 702 risk analytics firm.
Take 15 further vendors by seeded random selection from the important and standard tiers, minimum 30 in total.
Record seed, population size, selection date and tool for reproducibility.
Confirm the auditor owns no sampled relationship and does not sit in Procurement or Vendor Management.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all critical, ICT-critical and unregistered suppliers plus the Section 702 firm, and is free of self-review.

testing.step: Re-perform the criticality tiering judgement
actions: For each sampled vendor read the service description and independently decide whether its failure would stop claim payment, stop Exhibit F reporting, corrupt loan or valuation data, or impair the Available Asset calculation.
Reach your own tier before reading the recorded tier, then compare.
Treat every understated tier as an exception — an under-tiered vendor escapes the diligence and clause requirements entirely.
Record the PMIERs section each disputed vendor's failure would breach.
testing.done: each sampled vendor has an independent tier conclusion compared to the recorded tier, with every understatement raised as an exception.

testing.step: Test due-diligence currency and depth on the sample
actions: Open the diligence pack for each sampled critical vendor and confirm the SOC report period end is within 12 months of the test date.
Read the SOC report's exceptions and complementary user entity controls and confirm each CUEC has a named internal owner performing it.
Confirm financial-health, insurance and continuity evidence are present and dated.
Treat a filed-but-unread SOC report — no recorded findings, no CUEC ownership — as a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled critical vendor has diligence within 12 months with SOC exceptions recorded and CUECs owned internally.

testing.step: Test the mandatory PMIERs clauses in the sampled contracts
actions: Open each sampled critical contract and locate, clause by clause, audit and inspection rights extending to the Enterprises and FHFA, record retention, 24-hour incident notification, service levels, subcontracting consent, data location and exit assistance.
Compare what the executed document says to the clause metadata recorded in the CLM and flag every metadata overstatement.
Confirm any clause recorded as missing is under an executed amendment or a dated amendment plan with an interim mitigation.
Record the contract id, execution date and clause findings in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled critical contract has clause-by-clause findings from the executed document, with every CLM metadata overstatement flagged.

testing.step: Trace the Section 702 engagement and opinion end to end
actions: Confirm the Enterprise request, the firm the Enterprise selected, the engagement letter, the CRO approval and the cost borne by the insurer are all on file with dates.
Confirm the data package log lists every dataset supplied with its date, and reconcile the loan-level file supplied to the Exhibit F submission for the same as-of date.
Read the delivered opinion and confirm a documented management response exists for every finding, dated before the Enterprise discussion.
Confirm any capital effect implied by the opinion was quantified and reflected in the sufficiency ratio reporting.
testing.done: the Section 702 engagement traces from Enterprise request to opinion to management response with a reconciled data log and any capital effect quantified.

testing.step: Recompute the diligence, attestation and engagement clocks
actions: Recompute days since the last diligence report period end for every sampled critical vendor and compare to the 12-month standard.
Recompute attestation timeliness as attestation date minus quarter end and compare to the 10-business-day standard.
Recompute the Section 702 engagement start as engagement letter date minus Enterprise request date and compare to the 30-calendar-day standard.
Confirm the register pack was included in the quarterly submission at quarter end plus 45 calendar days and in the April 15 annual certification.
testing.done: diligence ages, attestation lags and the Section 702 engagement clock are all recomputed against their standards with day counts stated.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the vendor, the failed attribute (unregistered, under-tiered, stale diligence, missing clause, unattested, no exit plan) and the PMIERs impact.
Assign a root cause — engagement outside procurement, owner turnover, diligence never chased, clause waived at signature — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and an interim mitigation, including restricting data flow or holding payment for critical vendors operating with an open gap.
Carry every exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and an interim mitigation for critical vendors.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the third-party register test
actions: Compute the register completeness rate against GL spend, the critical-vendor diligence currency rate and the mandatory-clause coverage rate, and compare each to threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind each rate.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns no sampled relationship, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any unsubstitutable critical concentration to the Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the three rates against threshold, the conclusion and a Risk Committee reporting date.

checklist.step: Detect and declare the incident with a severity that survives scrutiny
actions: Open the incident record on the first credible signal from monitoring, the service desk, a vendor notification or a SIEM alert, and record the detection timestamp and source.
Apply the severity matrix on impact to claims payment, loan-level data integrity, Exhibit F reporting, investment data and borrower personal data — not on the number of users complaining.
Record the rationale for the severity in the incident record; any later downgrade requires a written rationale and the approval of the Operational Risk Manager.
Page the crisis bridge for severity-1 and notify the Operational Risk Manager, the Chief Information Officer and the Business Continuity Manager immediately.
checklist.done: the incident is declared with a timestamped detection record, a rationale-backed severity and the required immediate notifications sent.

checklist.step: Assess PMIERs materiality within 24 hours of declaration
actions: Complete the materiality test against four questions: does it impair claims payment; does it corrupt or expose loan-level, valuation or servicer data; does it threaten the quarter-end plus 45-day submission; does it change Available Assets, Minimum Required Assets or the sufficiency ratio.
Quantify the answer where possible — certificates affected, risk-in-force exposed, dollars of Available Assets in doubt, days of submission delay.
Record the determination as material or not material with the named decision-maker and the timestamp, inside 24 hours of declaration.
Where material, start the 30-calendar-day notification clock from the determination timestamp and inform the Chief Risk Officer the same day.
checklist.done: a timestamped, quantified materiality determination exists within 24 hours, and any material determination has started the 30-day clock.

checklist.step: Contain the incident and protect the loan-level and investment data
actions: Execute containment for the incident type — isolate affected hosts, revoke compromised credentials, halt the corrupting job, freeze the affected pipeline.
Preserve forensic evidence before remediation: capture logs, images and the affected dataset as it stood, and record chain of custody.
Suspend the Exhibit F pipeline and the investment position feed if their inputs may be corrupted, rather than publishing suspect data.
Record every containment action with its timestamp and the person who performed it.
checklist.done: containment actions are timestamped and logged, forensic evidence is preserved with chain of custody, and suspect data feeds are suspended rather than published.

checklist.step: Quantify the loan-level and reporting data impact
actions: Identify the affected records by certificate number, as-of date and field, and produce a count and total risk-in-force exposed.
Compare the affected fields to the Exhibit F specification and state which submitted reports contain wrong values and for which quarters.
Check whether any affected field feeds the Minimum Required Assets factor lookup — LTV, credit score, vintage, delinquency bucket — and tell the Capital Management Manager the same day if so.
Hand the impact statement to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for the resubmission decision.
checklist.done: the data impact is quantified by certificate count, risk-in-force and affected quarters, with capital-relevant fields flagged to Capital Management.

checklist.step: Draft the Enterprise notification with the facts, not reassurance
actions: Complete the notification template: event description, detection and determination timestamps, PMIERs sections engaged, systems and data affected, certificates and risk-in-force exposed, containment status, current effect on claims payment and reporting, and expected restoration date.
State plainly whether any submitted Exhibit F dataset or capital figure is affected and whether a corrected submission will follow, with a date.
Attach the interim update commitment — weekly for material incidents until closure.
Have the Chief Risk Officer approve the content before it goes to counsel.
checklist.done: a complete draft notification exists with timestamps, quantified exposure, submission impact and a CRO approval recorded.

checklist.step: Clear the notification through Regulatory Counsel and transmit inside 30 days
actions: Review the draft for accuracy, for statements that concede a PMIERs breach and for privilege over the forensic investigation.
Confirm the notification satisfies the master policy notification terms as well as the PMIERs expectation, and note any earlier deadline the master policy imposes.
Sign the clearance page and hand to Market Conduct Compliance for transmission to the Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac counterparty contacts through the secure channel.
Record the transmission timestamp and compute days used against the 30-calendar-day clock on the incident record.
checklist.done: the notification is counsel-cleared, transmitted through the secure channel inside 30 calendar days and the day count is recorded on the incident.

checklist.step: Keep the Enterprise updated until closure
actions: Send a written interim update weekly for every material incident, covering containment progress, revised exposure figures and any change to the restoration or resubmission date.
Log every Enterprise question and answer with dates, and route new questions to the incident commander rather than answering informally.
Correct any previously reported figure explicitly rather than silently restating it in a later update.
Stop the update cadence only on written Enterprise acknowledgement of the final report.
checklist.done: weekly interim updates exist for every material incident with corrections stated explicitly, ending only at written Enterprise acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Recover service and prove it before declaring resolution
actions: Restore the affected services and have the business owner — Claims or Regulatory Reporting — confirm a real end-to-end transaction succeeds before resolution is declared.
Confirm the Exhibit F pipeline and investment position feed produce output matching a known-good control total before they are unsuspended.
Record the restoration timestamp and compute the outage duration against the process RTO.
Keep the incident open until data correction and notification obligations are complete, not merely until systems are up.
checklist.done: resolution is declared only after a business-verified transaction and control-total match, with outage duration compared to RTO.

checklist.step: Correct the affected data and any submitted report
actions: Correct the affected loan-level records at source and re-run the Exhibit F extract for each affected quarter-end as-of date.
Reconcile the corrected extract to the in-force register and record the before and after certificate counts and risk-in-force.

Decide with the Chief Financial Officer whether a corrected submission is owed for prior quarters and, if so, deliver it inside the current quarter-end plus 45-calendar-day window with a covering explanation.
Tell the Capital Management Manager to restate Minimum Required Assets and the sufficiency ratio where corrected fields changed a factor band.
checklist.done: affected records are corrected at source, extracts re-run and reconciled, and any corrected submission and capital restatement is delivered or formally decided against.

checklist.step: Run the post-incident review with a real root cause
actions: Hold the review within 15 business days of resolution with the incident commander, the affected business owners and the vendor where one was involved.
Build the timeline from the incident record timestamps — detection, declaration, materiality determination, containment, notification, restoration — and compute each interval.
Identify the control that should have prevented or detected the incident and why it did not, naming the control rather than the person.
Record the detection gap explicitly: time from first technical indicator to declaration.
checklist.done: a post-incident review within 15 business days states the interval timeline, the named failed control and the quantified detection gap.

checklist.step: Raise and drive the corrective actions
actions: Raise a GRC issue per corrective action with an owner, a date and the control it strengthens — monitoring coverage, change control, vendor notification terms, pipeline validation.
Set dates inside 45 calendar days for actions preventing recurrence of a material incident.
Require evidence of the control operating, not a project completion note, before closure.
Report open actions from material incidents to the Risk Committee each quarter until closed.
checklist.done: every corrective action is an owned, dated GRC issue closed only on evidence of the control operating, with material-incident actions due inside 45 days.

checklist.step: Feed incident learning into the continuity plan and exercise programme
actions: Compare the incident's actual behaviour to the Section 313 plan assumptions — invocation trigger, RTO, workaround adequacy, contact reachability — and record every divergence.
Update the plan and the runbooks for each divergence and increment the version citing the incident id.
Add the incident's scenario to the next annual exercise calendar so the recovery path is tested, not assumed.
Report the plan changes to the Chief Operating Officer with the incident as the stated driver.
checklist.done: plan and runbook versions are incremented citing the incident id, and the incident scenario is on the next exercise calendar.

checklist.step: Report the incident position into the PMIERs reporting cycle
actions: Produce a quarterly summary of qualifying incidents with severity, materiality determination, notification date and days used, data impact and corrective action status.
Include it in the quarterly PMIERs submission package due within 45 calendar days of quarter end and in the April 15 annual certification pack.
Flag any incident notified late or still open past 90 days in red with the executive owner named.
Present the same summary to the Risk Committee.
checklist.done: a quarterly incident summary is included in the 45-day submission package and the April 15 pack, with late and aged incidents flagged and owned.

checklist.step: Close the incident only when every obligation is discharged
actions: Confirm before closure: service restored and business-verified, data corrected, any corrected submission delivered or formally decided against, Enterprise notified and acknowledged, post-incident review complete and corrective actions raised.
Sign the materiality determination and the final notification for every severity-1 and every data-integrity incident.
Return to the incident commander any closure request missing one of the above, naming the gap.
Record the closure date and the total incident duration.
checklist.done: no incident closes without CRO confirmation of restoration, data correction, Enterprise acknowledgement, review completion and raised corrective actions.

checklist.step: Archive the incident file under retention
actions: Snapshot the incident file — timeline, severity and materiality rationale, forensic index, notifications and acknowledgements, data impact and correction evidence, review and corrective actions — as one immutable record.
Apply 7-year-from-closure retention and preserve chain of custody notes for forensic material.
Index by incident id, severity, PMIERs section engaged and affected system so patterns can be analysed without reopening files.
Record the archive id on the incident record before final closure.
checklist.done: the incident is archived as one retention-labelled record indexed by id, severity, PMIERs section and affected system.

testing.step: Build the qualifying incident population for the quarter
actions: Extract every incident with severity 1 or 2 raised in the quarter, plus every incident of any severity tagged to the Claims Platform, the Exhibit F pipeline, the investment position feed or the Enterprise transmission channel.
Add vendor-notified incidents from the vendor records and security incidents from the SIEM/SOAR case list so incidents that never became ITSM records are captured.
Include incidents whose severity was downgraded after declaration — those are where notification obligations get lost.
Sign the population as complete and record extract date and counts by severity.
testing.done: the population combines ITSM, vendor and SIEM sources, includes downgraded incidents, and is signed complete with counts by severity.

testing.step: Reconcile the incident population to independent detection sources
actions: Pull high-priority alerts and availability outages for the critical systems for the same period from the SIEM and monitoring platform.
Match each to an incident record and list alerts and outages with no corresponding incident.
Compare service-desk major-incident logs and claims or reporting delay reports to the population for the same effect.
Drive every unmatched signal to a named cause rather than accepting it as noise.
testing.done: every high-priority alert and outage reconciles to an incident record, or its absence is explained by a named cause.

testing.step: Draw and document the incident sample
actions: Take 100% of severity-1 incidents, 100% of incidents assessed material, 100% of data-integrity incidents and 100% of downgraded incidents.
Take 10 further incidents by seeded random selection from the remainder, minimum 20 in total.
Record seed, population size, selection date and tool for reproducibility.
Confirm the auditor triaged, managed or signed off none of the sampled incidents.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all severity-1, material, data-integrity and downgraded incidents, and is free of self-review.

testing.step: Re-perform the severity and PMIERs materiality judgement
actions: Read the incident facts and apply the severity matrix and the four-question materiality test independently before reading the recorded determination.
Compare your conclusion to the record and treat any understatement — severity too low, material judged immaterial — as an exception.
For every downgrade, confirm a written rationale and Operational Risk Manager approval exist and pre-date the downgrade.
Where materiality was quantified, recompute certificates affected and risk-in-force exposed from the source data.
testing.done: each sampled incident has an independent severity and materiality conclusion with recomputed exposure figures, and every downgrade is approved and rationalised.

testing.step: Trace the Enterprise notification and acknowledgement
actions: For each material incident open the transmitted notification and confirm it names the event, the timestamps, the PMIERs sections engaged and the quantified exposure.
Confirm the counsel clearance page is signed and dated before the transmission timestamp.
Confirm the transmission confirmation and the Enterprise acknowledgement are both on file, and that weekly interim updates ran to acknowledgement of the final report.
Record notification id, transmission timestamp and acknowledgement date in the workpaper.
testing.done: every material incident traces to a counsel-cleared, transmitted, acknowledged notification with interim updates evidenced through to closure.

testing.step: Verify the data correction and any Exhibit F resubmission
actions: For each data-integrity incident re-run the affected-record query for the affected as-of dates and confirm the corrupt values no longer exist at source.
Compare the re-run Exhibit F output to the submitted file for each affected quarter and confirm the differences are exactly those the correction intended.
Confirm any corrected submission was delivered, or that a documented decision not to resubmit was taken by the Chief Financial Officer with a stated basis.
Confirm the Minimum Required Assets and sufficiency ratio were restated where a corrected field changed a factor band.
testing.done: corrupt values are gone at source, corrected extracts differ only as intended, and resubmission and capital restatement are evidenced or formally decided against.

testing.step: Recompute the incident clocks
actions: Recompute detection-to-declaration, declaration-to-materiality-determination and determination-to-notification from the raw timestamps in the incident record.
Compare the materiality interval to the 24-hour standard and the notification interval to the 30-calendar-day standard, stating hours and days used.
Check whether the master policy imposed an earlier notification deadline than 30 days and whether it was met.
Confirm any resubmission landed inside the quarter-end plus 45-calendar-day window.
testing.done: all four intervals are recomputed from raw timestamps and stated against their standards, including any earlier master policy deadline.

testing.step: Test whether post-incident actions actually closed on evidence
actions: For each sampled incident list the corrective actions with owner, due date and status and confirm each links to the incident id.
For closed actions open the closure evidence and confirm it shows the control operating, not a project completion note.
Confirm plan or runbook versions were incremented where the review identified a divergence, citing the incident id.
Check whether the same failed control appears in an earlier incident — a repeat is the finding, not the incident.
testing.done: every corrective action traces to closure evidence showing the control operating, with repeats of the same failed control identified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the incident id, the failed attribute (no materiality assessment, understated severity, late notification, uncorrected data, unevidenced closure) and the PMIERs impact.
Assign a root cause — triage matrix not applied, materiality task not routed, counsel clearance queued, data owner unidentified — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date inside 30 calendar days and open a self-disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel for any late Enterprise notification.
Carry every exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a 30-day date and, for late notifications, a counsel-led self-disclosure assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the incident notification test
actions: Compute the on-time materiality assessment rate, the on-time notification rate and the data-correction completion rate and compare each to threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each rate.
Have the independent reviewer, who managed no sampled incident, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any late Enterprise notification to the Audit Committee and the Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the three rates against threshold, the conclusion and the committee reporting dates.

checklist.step: Confirm the factor tables and amendment step in force for the quarter
actions: Open the current PMIERs text and Exhibit A on the Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac PMIERs pages and confirm the required-asset factor tables in force for the quarter-end as-of date.
Check the Enterprises' PMIERs FAQ and any amendment notices issued since the last quarter for changes to factors, delinquency treatment or the Available Asset standard.
Record the phase-in step of the 2024 Available Asset amendment applicable to this quarter and the remaining steps to full effectiveness on 9/30/2026.
Version-stamp the factor table file loaded into the calculation and record the source URL and download date so the version applied is provable.
checklist.done: the quarter's factor table version, its source and download date, and the applicable amendment phase-in step are recorded before any calculation runs.

checklist.step: Cut and reconcile the Exhibit F loan-level input
actions: Run the Exhibit F extract at the quarter-end as-of date with the fields the factor lookup needs: original LTV, representative credit score, vintage year, product type, occupancy, delinquency status bucket, modification flag and risk-in-force.
Reconcile certificate count and total risk-in-force to the policy administration in-force register and to the statutory Schedule of insurance in force, and clear differences above 0.1%.
Profile the file for nulls and out-of-range values in every factor-driving field and route defects to the Data Quality Manager before the file is released.
Publish the file with a run id and hash and notify Capital Management that the input is frozen.
checklist.done: a hashed, frozen Exhibit F extract is published, reconciled within 0.1% of risk-in-force and clean of nulls in every factor-driving field.

checklist.step: Apply the required-asset factors loan by loan
actions: Load the frozen Exhibit F file and the version-stamped factor tables and map each loan to its factor cell on LTV band, credit score band, vintage and performing or non-performing status.
Apply the delinquency and modification treatment the tables specify for each non-performing bucket rather than a blanket rate.
Compute gross required assets per loan as factor times risk-in-force and aggregate to portfolio, vintage and delinquency views.
Log every loan that failed to map to a factor cell and resolve each before aggregation; unmapped loans must never default to zero.
checklist.done: every loan maps to a factor cell with the correct delinquency treatment, gross required assets aggregate cleanly, and no loan defaulted to a zero factor.

checklist.step: Apply approved risk-transfer credit with its supporting evidence
actions: List every risk-transfer structure claimed for PMIERs credit — quota share, excess of loss, insurance-linked notes — with the Enterprise approval reference and effective dates.
Compute the credit each structure gives at the quarter-end as-of date under its attachment and detachment points and its remaining capacity.
Reconcile ceded risk-in-force in the reinsurance system to the ceded amounts in the statutory statement and the Exhibit F view.
Attach the Enterprise approval letter for each structure; unapproved structures take no credit, whatever their economics.
checklist.done: each claimed structure has an Enterprise approval reference, a computed credit at the as-of date and ceded amounts reconciled to the statutory statement.

checklist.step: Compute Minimum Required Assets and document every adjustment
actions: Build Minimum Required Assets as gross required assets less approved risk-transfer credit, plus any floor or minimum the tables impose.
List every manual adjustment on its own line with the basis, the PMIERs section or FAQ that permits it, the preparer and the dollar amount.
Produce a movement analysis against the prior quarter split by new insurance written, run-off, credit migration, delinquency movement and factor-table change.
Explain any movement above 2% of the prior quarter figure in writing before the number goes to review.
checklist.done: Minimum Required Assets is built with every manual adjustment individually justified and a movement analysis explaining changes above 2%.

checklist.step: Determine Available Assets under the amended standard
actions: Start from statutory admitted assets at quarter end and remove the items PMIERs excludes, listing each exclusion and its carrying value.

Classify remaining bonds by credit quality and liquidity tier under the amended standard, and separately identify holdings backed by residential mortgages or commercial real estate that carry haircuts or concentration limits.
Apply the haircut and limit at the phase-in step in force for the quarter and show the fully effective 9/30/2026 figure alongside it.
Tie the total back to Schedule D and the Exhibit of Assets in the statutory statement and document every bridging item.
checklist.done: Available Assets is built from statutory admitted assets with itemised exclusions, amendment-based tiering and haircuts at the correct phase-in step, tied to Schedule D.

checklist.step: Compute the sufficiency ratio and the headroom in dollars
actions: Compute the sufficiency ratio as Available Assets divided by Minimum Required Assets and state it to two decimal places.
Compute headroom in dollars above the 100% requirement and above the internal management buffer set by the board.
Restate both on the fully effective 9/30/2026 Available Asset basis so the phase-in is not hiding a future shortfall.
Produce the ratio trend for the last eight quarters with the drivers of each move annotated.
checklist.done: the ratio, dollar headroom against the 100% requirement and the internal buffer, and the fully effective 9/30/2026 restatement are all computed and trended.

checklist.step: Run the independent review before anything is certified
actions: Re-perform the factor lookup on an independent recalculation of at least 10% of risk-in-force, selected to cover every factor band in use.
Recompute Available Assets exclusions and haircuts independently from the position file rather than from the preparer's workbook.
Challenge every manual adjustment and every movement above 2% and record the preparer's response.
Sign the review with the differences found in dollars and the ratio effect, and withhold sign-off where a difference exceeds 0.5%.
checklist.done: a signed independent review exists covering at least 10% of risk-in-force with differences quantified in dollars and ratio effect.

checklist.step: Refresh the Section 701 capital plan on expected and severely adverse scenarios
actions: Project Minimum Required Assets and Available Assets over at least eight quarters on the expected scenario using the business plan's new insurance written, persistency and default assumptions.

Build the stress scenario on macroeconomic assumptions consistent with the Federal Reserve CCAR severely adverse scenario — house price decline path, unemployment path, interest rate path — and document the source and vintage of each path.
Show the projected sufficiency ratio quarter by quarter on both scenarios, on the phased and the fully effective 9/30/2026 Available Asset basis.
Where the stress path projects a shortfall, name the quarter it first appears and size the capital need in dollars.
checklist.done: an eight-quarter projection exists on expected and CCAR severely adverse paths, on both phase-in bases, with any first shortfall quarter and dollar need named.

checklist.step: Document the contingent capital actions behind the plan
actions: List the contingent actions available — holding company downstream, debt issuance, equity raise, additional quota share or excess-of-loss reinsurance, insurance-linked note issuance, new insurance written curtailment.
For each record the capacity in dollars, the lead time to execute, the approvals needed and any Enterprise approval required before PMIERs credit applies.
Sequence the actions against the projected shortfall quarter so execution starts ahead of the need, not at it.
Confirm with the Chief Investment Officer that the asset mix supporting the plan stays inside the amended Available Asset limits after each action.
checklist.done: each contingent action has capacity, lead time, approval path and a start date sequenced ahead of the projected shortfall quarter.

checklist.step: Take the calculation and plan through governance
actions: Present the quarterly ratio, movement analysis, review findings and the stress projection to the Asset-Liability and Capital Committee before submission.
Take the annual capital plan to the board for approval, with the CCAR severely adverse assumptions and the contingent action sequence explicit.
Record the committee and board decisions, challenges and any assumption changed as a result, in the minutes.
File the approved plan and minutes to the board portal and to the Section 701 readiness index row.
checklist.done: the quarterly ratio is committee-reviewed and the annual plan board-approved, with challenges and assumption changes recorded in the minutes.

checklist.step: Certify and submit inside the 45-day window
actions: Sign the quarterly PMIERs certification confirming the calculation follows the factor tables and the Available Asset standard in force, alongside the Chief Executive Officer for the annual certification.
Confirm the submission package contains the Exhibit F dataset, the calculation summary, the Available Asset schedule and the ratio before transmission.
Transmit through the Enterprise secure channel by quarter end plus 45 calendar days, and by April 15 for the annual certification.
Capture the transmission confirmation and record days used against both deadlines.
checklist.done: the certification is signed and the full package transmitted inside 45 calendar days of quarter end, and by April 15 annually, with confirmations stored.

checklist.step: Reconcile the submitted figures back to the statutory statement
actions: Tie Available Assets to statutory surplus, Schedule D and the Exhibit of Assets in the quarterly or annual statement for the same as-of date and document each bridging item.
Tie risk-in-force and ceded risk-in-force to the statutory schedules for insurance in force and to the reinsurance schedules.
Explain every bridging item in writing — contingency reserve treatment, non-admitted assets, deferred tax — with the amount.
Have the Controller countersign the reconciliation before it is filed with the calculation pack.
checklist.done: Available Assets and risk-in-force tie to the statutory statement with every bridging item explained and countersigned by the Controller.

checklist.step: Correct and resubmit when an error is found after submission
actions: Quantify the error's effect on Minimum Required Assets, Available Assets and the ratio for every affected quarter.
Take the correction and the resubmission decision to the Chief Financial Officer the same week the error is identified.
Where the corrected ratio would have fallen below 100% in any submitted quarter, notify the Enterprises without waiting for the next cycle and open a remediation plan.
Log the error as a GRC exception with root cause, dollar effect and the control change that prevents recurrence.
checklist.done: the error's ratio effect is quantified by quarter, a CFO resubmission decision is recorded, and any sub-100% restatement is notified immediately.

checklist.step: Archive the calculation pack under retention
actions: Snapshot the quarter's pack — factor table version, hashed Exhibit F input, calculation workbooks, risk-transfer support, Available Asset classification, review sign-off, certification and transmission confirmation — as one immutable record.
Apply 7-year retention and preserve the input hash so a future reviewer can prove which data produced the submitted ratio.
Index by quarter, entity, ratio and factor table version.
Record the archive id on the Section 703 readiness index row.
checklist.done: the quarter's calculation pack is archived with its input hash, retention-labelled and indexed by quarter, ratio and factor table version.

testing.step: Build the calculation population and its inputs
actions: Obtain the hashed Exhibit F extract used in the submission, the version-stamped factor tables, the position file, the risk-transfer schedule and the submitted calculation workbook.
Confirm the hash on the extract you received matches the hash recorded at freeze — a re-run file is not the submitted file.
Record row counts, total risk-in-force, position count and market value as the population control totals.
Sign the population as complete and record the receipt date and source of each input.
testing.done: every input is received with a hash or version matching the submission record, and control totals are captured and signed.

testing.step: Reconcile the inputs to the source of record
actions: Reconcile Exhibit F risk-in-force and certificate count independently to the policy administration in-force register and to the statutory insurance-in-force schedule.
Reconcile the position file market value to Schedule D and the Exhibit of Assets for the same as-of date.
Reconcile ceded risk-in-force to the statutory reinsurance schedules and the reinsurance administration system.
Investigate every variance above 0.1% to named certificates or positions.
testing.done: all three inputs reconcile to the statutory statement and the systems of record within 0.1%, with named-item explanations for variances.

testing.step: Draw and document the loan and position sample
actions: Take a stratified sample of 60 loans covering every factor band in use, including non-performing and modified buckets and the highest-LTV and lowest-score cells.
Take 100% of positions backed by residential mortgages or commercial real estate and the 25 largest other holdings.
Take 100% of risk-transfer structures and 100% of manual adjustments.
Record seed, stratification basis, population size and selection date for reproducibility.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers every factor band, all mortgage- and CRE-backed positions, all structures and all manual adjustments.

testing.step: Re-perform the factor lookup independently
actions: For each sampled loan read LTV, credit score, vintage, product and delinquency status from the Exhibit F record and select the factor cell yourself from the version-stamped table.
Compute required assets as factor times risk-in-force and compare to the model output loan by loan.
Confirm the delinquency and modification treatment applied matches the table's rules for that bucket rather than a blended rate.
Extrapolate any systematic difference across the affected band and quantify the portfolio effect in dollars.
testing.done: every sampled loan has an independently selected factor and recomputed required assets, with any systematic difference extrapolated in dollars.

testing.step: Re-perform the Available Asset classification and phase-in haircut
actions: For each sampled position independently assign credit-quality and liquidity tier from the position record and the rating source, not from the preparer's workbook.
Recompute the amendment haircut at the phase-in step in force for the quarter and compare to the applied haircut.
Recompute the residential-mortgage and commercial-real-estate concentration tests and state headroom or breach in dollars.
Recompute the fully effective 9/30/2026 figure and confirm it matches the figure shown alongside the phased number.
testing.done: sampled positions are independently tiered, haircuts and concentration tests recompute to the workbook, and the 9/30/2026 figure agrees.

testing.step: Test the risk-transfer credit and every manual adjustment
actions: For each structure confirm the Enterprise approval letter exists, covers the quarter tested and matches the structure as executed in the treaty documents.
Recompute the credit at the as-of date from attachment and detachment points and remaining capacity, and compare to the credit taken.
For each manual adjustment read the documented basis and the PMIERs section or FAQ cited, and confirm it permits the adjustment.
Treat any adjustment supported only by preparer judgement as an exception with its full dollar amount.
testing.done: every structure has a valid Enterprise approval and a recomputed credit, and every manual adjustment has a cited, verified basis.

testing.step: Trace the submitted figures to evidence and identifiers
actions: Open the transmitted submission package and confirm the Minimum Required Assets, Available Assets and ratio in it match the reviewed and certified workbook exactly.
Confirm the certification carries the Chief Financial Officer signature and, for the annual, the Chief Executive Officer signature with dates.
Confirm the independent review sign-off pre-dates the certification and covers at least 10% of risk-in-force.
Record workbook version, review sign-off date, certification date and transmission confirmation id in the workpaper.
testing.done: submitted figures match the certified workbook exactly, with review sign-off pre-dating certification and all identifiers recorded.

testing.step: Recompute the ratio, the movement and the deadline maths
actions: Recompute the sufficiency ratio from your independently derived Minimum Required Assets and Available Assets and compare to the submitted ratio to two decimal places.
Recompute the quarter-on-quarter movement split and confirm the explanations given account for the whole movement, not most of it.
Recompute the submission deadline as quarter end plus 45 calendar days and compare to the transmission timestamp; do the same for the April 15 annual certification.
Confirm the recomputed ratio stays above 100% and above the board buffer, and quantify the headroom.
testing.done: the ratio, movement split and both deadlines are recomputed and stated, with headroom against 100% and the board buffer quantified.

testing.step: Test the capital plan's stress assumptions and shortfall logic
actions: Confirm the severely adverse house price, unemployment and rate paths trace to the published Federal Reserve CCAR severely adverse scenario of the stated vintage, path point by path point.
Re-run the projection with the documented assumptions and confirm the projected quarterly ratios reproduce within tolerance.
Confirm the projection is shown on the fully effective 9/30/2026 Available Asset basis as well as the phased basis.
Confirm each contingent action's capacity and lead time are evidenced and that the sequence starts before the projected shortfall quarter.
testing.done: the stress paths trace to the published CCAR scenario, the projection reproduces, and contingent actions are evidenced and sequenced ahead of the shortfall.

testing.step: Log exceptions, then conclude, sign and report
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception with the dollar effect on Minimum Required Assets, Available Assets and the ratio, a root cause and a named owner with a date inside 30 calendar days.
Compute the aggregate difference as a percentage of the submitted Minimum Required Assets and Available Assets and compare to the 0.5% threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — and have the independent reviewer, who prepared no part of the calculation, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, the recomputed ratio and any restatement need to the Audit Committee and the Chief Financial Officer, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: every exception is logged with its dollar and ratio effect, and a signed workpaper states the aggregate difference against 0.5%, the conclusion and the reporting dates.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarter-end ratio reported to the Enterprises within 45 calendar days; monthly interim estimate to the Asset-Liability and Capital Committee by working day 10; amber or red trigger escalated to the CFO within 1 business day and a remediation plan to the Enterprises within 30 calendar days of a breach determination; annual certification April 15

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Fail if a monthly estimate was missed or produced after working day 10, if a trigger crossing was not escalated within 1 business day, if a threshold was changed without Risk Committee approval, or if a breach was not notified to the Enterprises within 30 calendar days; any breach handling failure escalates to the board Risk Committee
