checklist.step: Set the trigger ladder and get it board-approved
actions: Define the ladder in ratio terms: green above the board buffer, amber between the buffer and a defined warning level, red between the warning level and 100%, breach below 100%.
Set the buffer with reference to the CCAR severely adverse projection so the buffer absorbs the modelled stress rather than being a round number.
Define a second ladder on the fully effective 9/30/2026 Available Asset basis so the phase-in cannot mask a forward breach.
Take both ladders to the board Risk Committee for approval and record the approved levels and effective date in the minutes.
checklist.done: both trigger ladders are board-approved with levels, rationale and effective date recorded in the Risk Committee minutes.

checklist.step: Configure the monitoring dashboard and lock the thresholds
actions: Build the dashboard to show the ratio, Available Assets, Minimum Required Assets and dollar headroom, on both the phased and fully effective 9/30/2026 bases.
Load the approved threshold values as controlled parameters with change history, and restrict edit rights to a named administrator outside Capital Management.
Configure alerts to the Chief Financial Officer, Chief Risk Officer and Head of Capital Management on any crossing into amber, red or breach.
Record the data lineage on the dashboard — ledger extract, position file and loan-level warehouse job ids and refresh times — so a viewer can tell how stale the number is.
checklist.done: the dashboard shows both bases with locked, change-logged thresholds, configured alerts and visible data lineage and refresh times.

checklist.step: Produce the monthly interim ratio estimate by working day 10
actions: Roll Minimum Required Assets forward from the last quarter-end using the month's new insurance written, cancellations, delinquency movement and any factor-band migration from the loan-level warehouse.
Roll Available Assets forward using the month-end ledger position, investment market value movement and the amendment tiering and haircuts at the current phase-in step.
Compute the estimated ratio on both bases, document the approximations made, and state the estimate's expected accuracy range.
Publish to the dashboard and to the Asset-Liability and Capital Committee by working day 10 with the drivers of the month's move annotated.
checklist.done: a documented monthly estimate on both bases is published by working day 10 with approximations, accuracy range and move drivers stated.

checklist.step: Reconcile each monthly estimate back to the last actual
actions: Compare the prior month's estimate to the subsequent quarter-end actual and compute the estimation error in ratio points and dollars.
Attribute the error to its source — loan-level roll-forward, market value movement, exclusion treatment, factor-band migration.
Adjust the estimation method where an error source repeats across two months rather than treating each miss as noise.
Record the running estimation accuracy so the committee knows how much weight the interim number carries.
checklist.done: each estimate is back-tested against the quarter-end actual with attributed error and a recorded running accuracy.

checklist.step: Run early-warning indicators ahead of the ratio itself
actions: Monitor leading indicators monthly: 60+ day delinquency rate by vintage, house price index movement in the largest state concentrations, new insurance written mix shifting to higher-factor bands, investment credit migration and unrealised loss position.
Set an amber level on each indicator and report crossings even when the ratio itself is still green.
Model the ratio effect of each crossing so an indicator move is expressed in ratio points, not just direction.
Report the indicator dashboard alongside the ratio to the Asset-Liability and Capital Committee monthly.
checklist.done: every leading indicator has an amber level, and crossings are reported monthly with their modelled ratio effect in points.

checklist.step: Escalate a trigger crossing within one business day
actions: On any amber or red alert, confirm the crossing is real by validating the underlying data refresh before escalating — but escalate inside one business day either way.

Notify the Chief Financial Officer and the Chief Risk Officer in writing with the ratio, the driver, the dollar headroom and whether the crossing appears on the phased basis, the 9/30/2026 basis or both.
Open a GRC trigger event record with the crossing timestamp, level, driver and the named owner of the response.
Convene the Asset-Liability and Capital Committee within 5 business days for a red crossing.
checklist.done: every crossing has a written escalation inside one business day, a GRC trigger record and, for red, a committee meeting inside 5 business days.

checklist.step: Build the management response sized to the trigger level
actions: For amber, tighten monitoring to weekly, defer discretionary capital actions and pre-position the fastest contingent action from the Section 701 plan.
For red, execute a named contingent action from the plan — reinsurance placement, holding company downstream, new insurance written curtailment — with an execution date.
Size the action against the dollar gap to the board buffer, not the gap to 100%, so restoration clears the buffer.
Record the decision, the sizing and the owner in the committee minutes the same week.
checklist.done: the response is sized in dollars to restore above the board buffer, names a contingent action with an execution date, and is minuted.

checklist.step: Suspend capital outflows while a trigger is live
actions: Freeze dividends, intercompany distributions and discretionary share repurchase from the mortgage guaranty entity on any red crossing.
Confirm no distribution is executed without written Chief Financial Officer release and, where applicable, the domiciliary regulator's approval for an extraordinary dividend.
Recheck that any planned investment action keeps the portfolio inside the amended Available Asset tiering and concentration limits before it is executed.
Record the freeze, its scope and its release date on the trigger event record.
checklist.done: outflows are frozen on a red crossing with scope and release dates recorded, and no distribution proceeds without written CFO release.

checklist.step: Determine and document a breach the moment the ratio falls below 100%
actions: Confirm the sub-100% figure from validated data rather than a dashboard estimate, and record the determination timestamp.
State whether the breach is on the phased basis, the fully effective 9/30/2026 basis or both, and the dollar shortfall in each case.
Notify the Chief Executive Officer and the board chair the same day and convene the board Risk Committee inside 5 business days.
Start the 30-calendar-day clock for delivering a remediation plan to the Enterprises from the determination timestamp.
checklist.done: the breach is determined from validated data with a timestamp, basis and dollar shortfall, notified to CEO and board chair the same day.

checklist.step: Notify the Enterprises and deliver the remediation plan
actions: Draft the notification with the ratio, the shortfall in dollars, the drivers, the actions already taken and the plan to restore compliance with dates.
Route it through Regulatory Counsel for clearance and Market Conduct Compliance for transmission to the Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac counterparty contacts.
Deliver the remediation plan within 30 calendar days of the determination, naming the capital actions, their capacity, their execution dates and the projected quarter of restoration.
Record the transmission confirmation and days used on the trigger event record.
checklist.done: the breach notification and a dated remediation plan are counsel-cleared and transmitted inside 30 calendar days, with confirmations stored.

checklist.step: Track remediation to restoration with weekly evidence
actions: Break the plan into actions with owner, dollar contribution, execution date and any Enterprise approval needed before PMIERs credit applies.
Report weekly to the Chief Financial Officer on executed dollars against planned dollars and the resulting projected ratio.
Send the Enterprises a written progress update at the cadence agreed in the plan, correcting prior figures explicitly where they change.
Keep the trigger record open until the ratio is above the board buffer on validated quarter-end data, not on an estimate.
checklist.done: remediation actions are tracked weekly in dollars executed versus planned, with agreed Enterprise updates, until a validated quarter-end ratio clears the buffer.

checklist.step: Report the ratio position into governance every cycle
actions: Report monthly to the Asset-Liability and Capital Committee: ratio on both bases, headroom in dollars, indicator crossings and estimation accuracy.
Report quarterly to the board Risk Committee with the eight-quarter trend, the CCAR severely adverse projection and the distance to the first projected shortfall quarter.
Flag explicitly each quarter how much of the current headroom disappears at full effectiveness on 9/30/2026.
Record challenges and decisions in the minutes and carry actions into the GRC platform.
checklist.done: monthly committee and quarterly board reporting both occurred, with the 9/30/2026 headroom effect flagged and decisions minuted.

checklist.step: Control changes to thresholds and to the monitoring calculation
actions: Require every threshold change to carry a Risk Committee approval reference, an effective date and a before-and-after value in the change log.
Require every change to the estimation method or the dashboard calculation to be reviewed by the Capital Model Actuary and recorded with a version number.
Run a quarterly comparison of the live dashboard thresholds against the board-approved values and investigate any difference the same day.
Block edit rights for anyone who produces the estimates.
checklist.done: every threshold and method change carries an approval reference and version, and the live configuration matches the board-approved values each quarter.

checklist.step: Rehearse the breach response before it is needed
actions: Run an annual tabletop with the Chief Financial Officer, Chief Risk Officer, Treasury, Reinsurance and Regulatory Counsel on a sudden sub-100% scenario driven by a house price shock.
Time the group to a determination, a board notification, a drafted Enterprise notification and a sized remediation plan.
Test whether the fastest contingent action could actually execute inside the plan's stated lead time, by asking Treasury and Reinsurance to evidence it.
Log every gap the rehearsal exposes as a GRC issue with an owner and a date.
checklist.done: an annual breach rehearsal produced timed outcomes, evidenced contingent-action lead times and a logged gap list with owners.

checklist.step: Archive the monitoring record under retention
actions: Snapshot each quarter's monitoring record — monthly estimates and inputs, dashboard threshold configuration and change log, trigger events, escalations, board minutes and any remediation plan — as one immutable record.
Apply 7-year retention so the ratio history and the response to any past trigger can be evidenced to the Enterprises.
Index by quarter, ratio, trigger level and basis (phased or fully effective) so trend and breach questions are answerable without reopening files.
Record the archive id on the Section 701 and 703 readiness index rows.
checklist.done: each quarter's monitoring record is archived, retention-labelled and indexed by quarter, ratio, trigger level and phase-in basis.

testing.step: Build the population of estimates, ratios and trigger events
actions: Extract every monthly interim estimate and every quarter-end ratio in the period on both the phased and fully effective 9/30/2026 bases, with publication dates.
Extract every dashboard alert fired and every GRC trigger event record with crossing timestamps and levels.
Identify months where no estimate was published — the gaps are part of the population, not an absence of data.
Sign the population as complete and record extract date, estimate count and trigger count by level.
testing.done: the population lists every estimate, ratio and trigger event with missing months shown explicitly, signed complete.

testing.step: Reconcile reported ratios to the certified quarter-end calculation
actions: Compare each quarter-end ratio shown on the dashboard and in committee packs to the certified figure in the submitted PMIERs package.
Confirm Available Assets and Minimum Required Assets on the dashboard tie to the certified workbook, not to a later restated version.
Reconcile the dashboard's underlying ledger and position extracts to the general ledger and Schedule D for the same as-of date.
Explain every difference to a named cause — timing, restatement, basis — rather than tolerance.
testing.done: every reported quarter-end ratio ties to the certified submission with all differences explained by a named cause.

testing.step: Draw and document the monitoring sample
actions: Take 100% of amber, red and breach trigger events, 100% of threshold changes and 100% of quarter-end ratios in the period.
Take 6 monthly estimates by seeded random selection, minimum 12 items in total.
Record seed, population size, selection date and tool for reproducibility.
Confirm the reviewer produced none of the sampled estimates and sits outside Capital Management and Finance.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all trigger events, threshold changes and quarter-end ratios, and is free of self-review.

testing.step: Re-perform the monthly estimate from source data
actions: For each sampled month rebuild the Minimum Required Assets roll-forward from the loan-level warehouse movement and the factor tables in force, independently of the analyst's workbook.
Rebuild Available Assets from the month-end ledger and position file, applying the amendment tiering and the correct phase-in haircut.
Compute the ratio on both bases and compare to the published estimate in ratio points.
Confirm the published estimate's stated accuracy range actually contained the subsequent quarter-end actual.
testing.done: each sampled estimate is independently rebuilt and compared in ratio points, with the stated accuracy range tested against the actual.

testing.step: Verify the dashboard thresholds against board approval
actions: Read the board Risk Committee minutes approving the trigger ladders and record the approved levels and effective dates.
Compare them to the live dashboard threshold parameters and to the change log entries for the period.
Confirm each change carries an approval reference and that no change pre-dates its approval.
Confirm edit rights exclude everyone who produces the estimates, by inspecting the access list rather than the policy.
testing.done: live thresholds match board-approved levels with every change approved in advance, and the inspected access list excludes estimate producers.

testing.step: Trace every trigger crossing to its escalation and response
actions: For each sampled crossing open the alert record and the escalation email and record both timestamps.
Confirm the GRC trigger event exists with level, driver, dollar headroom and named response owner.
For red crossings confirm an Asset-Liability and Capital Committee meeting occurred inside 5 business days with minutes, and that outflows were frozen.
Confirm the trigger was stood down only on a validated quarter-end ratio above the board buffer, not on an estimate.
testing.done: every sampled crossing traces to a timestamped escalation, a complete trigger record, the required meeting, and a validated stand-down.

testing.step: Test breach notification and remediation where a breach occurred
actions: Confirm the breach determination is supported by validated data with a recorded timestamp and the basis and shortfall stated.
Confirm same-day notification to the Chief Executive Officer and board chair and a board Risk Committee meeting inside 5 business days with minutes.
Open the transmitted Enterprise notification and remediation plan and confirm counsel clearance pre-dates transmission.
Trace remediation actions to executed evidence — placed reinsurance, received downstream, curtailed new insurance written — and compare executed dollars to plan.
testing.done: the breach traces from validated determination through same-day internal notification to a counsel-cleared Enterprise plan with executed-versus-planned dollars.

testing.step: Recompute the escalation and notification clocks
actions: Recompute escalation timeliness as escalation timestamp minus alert timestamp and compare to the 1-business-day standard.
Recompute monthly estimate timeliness as publication date minus month end and compare to the working-day-10 standard.
Recompute the breach notification interval as transmission date minus determination date and compare to the 30-calendar-day standard.
Confirm each quarter-end ratio was reported within 45 calendar days of quarter end and that the April 15 annual certification carried the same basis and figure.
testing.done: all four clocks are recomputed from raw timestamps and stated against their standards with day counts.

testing.step: Test the forward view for a masked shortfall
actions: Recompute the current ratio on the fully effective 9/30/2026 Available Asset basis and compare to the phased ratio, stating the headroom lost in dollars and ratio points.
Re-run the CCAR severely adverse projection on the 9/30/2026 basis and identify the first quarter the projected ratio falls below the board buffer and below 100%.
Confirm the reporting to the committee and board disclosed that same quarter rather than a later one.
Flag as an exception any period where the phased ratio sat green while the 9/30/2026 basis sat amber or worse without disclosure.
testing.done: the 9/30/2026 basis is recomputed with headroom loss quantified, and any undisclosed forward amber or breach is raised as an exception.

testing.step: Log exceptions, then conclude, sign and report
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the month or event, the failed attribute (estimate missed or late, crossing not escalated, threshold changed without approval, late breach notification, undisclosed forward shortfall) and the capital impact.
Assign a root cause and an owner at executive level with a remediation date inside 30 calendar days.
Compute the estimate timeliness rate, the escalation timeliness rate and the estimate accuracy against the quarter-end actual, and compare each to threshold.

Write the conclusion, have the independent reviewer outside Capital Management and Finance sign and date the workpaper, report to the board Risk Committee and file it in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: every exception is logged with an executive owner and a 30-day date, and a signed workpaper states the three rates, the conclusion and the board Risk Committee reporting date.
